title: Voluntary Housing Refund
description: Allows you to return any CPF savings used for your home purchase to your CPF account while still owning your property. Doing so reduces the refund amount you would have to make and increases the cash proceeds you would get when you eventually sell or transfer your property. This also boosts your retirement savings as you can benefit from CPF interest rates.
highlights: Grow your retirement savings with CPF interest rates
Greater cash proceeds and lower required CPF refund upon property sale or transfer

sections.About this support:
- Receive more cash proceeds and refund less to your CPF account when selling or transferring your property
- Take advantage of CPF’s interest rates and retire with more
- Re-use CPF savings for the various CPF approved schemes if needed
sections.Who is this for?:
- You have used your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to purchase your property
- Please note the following conditions when making the voluntary housing refund:
  - You can refund up to the CPF principal amount withdrawn towards the property plus its accrued interest to your CPF account
  - If you are an undischarged bankrupt, you have to obtain the Official Assignee’s approval to make this housing refund
  - While housing grants will generally be refunded to your OA if you have an HDB flat, the grant(s) may be partially credited to your Special Account / Retirement Account and MediSave Account if you have received more than $30,000 in grant(s)
  - If you are 55 and above, the refunded amount [will be used to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS)](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/VHRAge55), which supports your retirement needs through monthly payouts
  - Any refunds beyond your cohort’s FRS will remain in your OA
- You can read more on [housing refunds and their processes](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/sales-proceeds-after-selling-your-home)
sections.How to apply?:
Check the amount of voluntary refund you can make under the “What happens if” section in your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard).

You can make the voluntary housing refund through the following methods:

- Log in to [my cpf digital services](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/make-a-voluntary-housing-refund) using your Singpass:
  - Choose your property and enter a refund amount

Or

- Use the CPF Mobile app:
  - Download the CPF Mobile app
  - Log in with your Singpass
  - Tap on 'Services'
  - Choose 'Voluntary Housing Refund'

title: Home Protection Scheme (HPS)
description: Mortgage-reducing insurance that protects you and your loved ones from losing your Housing and Development Board (HDB) flat in the event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability.
highlights: Payout up to the sum assured will be made to HDB or the mortgagee directly
Processing of claim application generally takes 5 working days upon CPF Board's receipt of requested documents

sections.About this support:
**For claims under death grounds**

- HPS benefits will be paid in a lump sum (based on the share of HPS cover) to HDB or the mortgagee directly to settle the outstanding housing loan.
  - Any excess claim amounts will be paid to the insured member's CPF Ordinary Account.
  - Thereafter, the deceased member’s CPF savings will be distributed to nominees, or next-of-kins depending on whether there is a valid nomination made.

**For claims admitted under medical grounds**

- Housing instalments (based on the share of HPS cover) may be paid by HPS for a period of up to two years, before a review of insured member's eligibility to claim the remaining insured sum in full is carried out.
sections.Who is this for?:
CPF members who own a HDB flat and are HPS policyholders paying their monthly housing instalments using CPF savings or cash are eligible to apply for HPS coverage.

- HPS claim payout is made to:
  - Next-of-kin of HPS policyholder who is deceased, or
  - HPS policyholder who is certified by a registered medical practitioner under the Medical Registration Act to be suffering from:
    - Terminal illness: an illness that is likely to result in the death of the insured CPF member within 12 months
    - Total permanent disability: the inability to take part in any employment permanently, or the total permanent loss of physical function of any of the following:
      - Both eyes, or
      - Two limbs, or
      - One eye and one limb
sections.How to apply?:
[Apply online for HPS coverage](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-adjust-home-protection-scheme-cover) via the CPF website with your Singpass.

**Claim on death grounds**

- If the insured member has an outstanding housing loan, CPF Board will automatically assess the deceased’s claim eligibility upon Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s notification.
- CPF Board will inform the co-owner(s) or the insured's next-of-kin of the outcome and if additional information is required.

**Claim on medical grounds**

- Submit your application to CPF Board directly via the [CPF website](http://cpf.gov.sg/applyrleandclaimhpsdps)

title: CPF Housing Scheme
description: Enables CPF members to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to buy properties and pay for various housing purchase-related costs if they are owners of the property.
highlights: Use CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to buy properties or pay for housing purchase-related costs

sections.About this support:
- Enables members to use their OA savings to buy residential property in Singapore
- OA savings can be used to cover downpayments, housing loans, stamp and legal fees and Home Protection Scheme premiums (for HDB flats)
sections.Who is this for?:
- The amount of OA savings members can use depends on several factors, including the remaining lease of the property, the type of housing loan you’re taking, the age of the youngest owner using CPF, and the number of properties you are using CPF for
- For detailed information on the terms and conditions, please refer to the [terms and conditions for use of CPF savings under the CPF Housing Scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tnc/t-c-for-use-of-cpf-under-cpf-housing-scheme)
- Upon sale, transfer or disposal of the property (during your lifetime), you are required to refund the CPF principal amount withdrawn together with the accrued interest to your CPF account(s)
- If you are aged 55 or above and have pledged the property to make up your retirement sum, you will also be required to refund the pledged amount
sections.How to apply?:
- To use your OA savings for the property, HDB or the lawyer acting for you in the purchase must submit an application to the CPF Board with your CPF withdrawal details, along with any required documentation
- [Know how much OA you can use](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home)
- Before your OA savings can be used, you may need to pay certain amounts in cash, [depending on the type of property and housing loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/can-i-use-my-cpf-savings-for-the-down-payment-of-my-property)
- Note that the savings withdrawn are paid to the property developer, HDB, sellers, banks, lawyers or such other entities on your behalf
- To adjust or stop your OA savings for your loan payments, log in to your HDB e-Services if you have an HDB loan or [myCPF](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/houseinstalment) if you have a bank loan

title: CPF Education Loan Scheme
description: A loan scheme that allows CPF member to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs).
highlights: Allows for the use of OA savings to pay for the government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)
Applications will only be processed after the application period for the approved educational institution has closed
Processing of application generally takes 3 working days upon receipt of the student's enrolment confirmation from the approved educational institution

sections.About this support:
- Allows the use of OA savings to pay for own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for [full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- The student (i.e., borrower) would need to start repaying the principal amount withdrawn plus the accrued interest in cash, to the lender’s CPF OA, one year after graduating from or leaving the course of study, whichever occurs earlier

Note:

- OA savings can be used up to the Available Withdrawal Limit under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is either 40% of your accumulated OA savings, or your remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The amount that can be used is also subject to the tuition fees payable
- If you are 55 or older, you must set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account before using the remaining OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit.
- You may wish to check how much tuition fees can be paid using [OA savings.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-of-tuition-fees-can-be-paid-using-cpf-ordinary-account-oa-savings)
sections.Who is this for?:
- CPF members/lenders with OA savings are eligible to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, or relative’s government subsidised tuition fees using OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is up to 40% of accumulated OA savings, or the remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The CPF member can check the Available Withdrawal Limit through the CPF website using Singpass
- Only full-time diploma / degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs) are covered under this loan scheme
- For the list of approved courses, you may refer to [approved courses under this scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- Here are the alternative education financing options:
  - [MOE Higher Education Student Loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-is-the-moe-higher-education-student-loan-hesl)
  - [Other financing options offered by the institutions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-are-the-financing-options-from-moe-and-the-educational-institutions)
  - [Post-Secondary Education Account funds](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea)
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply online through [“Forms and e-applications"](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications) at [CPF website](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan) with your Singpass
- You must read the accompanying Terms & Conditions, and Procedures & Guidelines before you complete the online form
- Before you submit your application online under the CPF Education Loan Scheme:
  - Check the application period for the approved educational institution you are applying to use CPF savings to pay your tuition fees
  - Ensure you are accepted by the institution and confirm that it is an approved educational institution under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
  - Establish whether you are a new (e.g. fresh intake for AY2024/2025) or existing student (e.g. 2nd year student) under the institution
- You are required to submit 1 (one) application form for each CPF lender, for the entire course of study, unless you enrol into a different AEI
- Please note the application period for use of CPF savings under CPF Education Loan Scheme differs for each AEI
- You may [refer to their schedules here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan/application-schedule)

title: Youth COP
description: Aims to foster positive development and strengthen protective factors, empowering youths as crime-prevention leaders to help their communities thrive, stay safe, and build resilience.

sections.About this support:
Youth COP is a 3-year developmental programme that empowers students to become confident, responsible crime-prevention leaders who help keep their peers and communities safe. In partnership with Neighbourhood Police Centres and selected schools, the programme develops youths into active contributors who serve, protect, and care for their community through meaningful engagement and public education efforts.

Through strong collaboration with families, schools, police, and the wider community, Youth COP equips students with leadership skills, crime-prevention knowledge, and opportunities to make a positive impact. As Crime Prevention Ambassadors, participants build a strong sense of identity and self-worth, gain the competencies to navigate life’s challenges, make informed decisions, and foster safer, more caring school and community environments.
sections.Who is this for?: The programme supports secondary school students in selected schools, with leadership potential by providing guidance, developmental opportunities, and the knowledge and skills to understand laws and their implications. Youth COP nurtures these young people into positive contributors within their schools and communities, grounded in the belief that all youths grow and thrive when supported with strong relationships, meaningful experiences, and opportunities to realise their potential.
sections.How to apply?:
- Students can nominate themselves through the booths in school.
- Students can also be nominated for the programme through school personnel (e.g. teachers).
sections.What to expect?:
- Programme staff will conduct a selection interview with the nominated student (by self or other school referral)  Students will be assessed for their risks, needs and suitability for this programme, within 2 to 3 weeks of referral or sign-up.
- In the event that student is not suitable for the programme, they will be given a letter to explain reasons for rejection and will be directed to other services based on the social worker's recommendations.

title: Shared Parental Leave  (SPL)
description: Support eligible working parents in sharing parental responsibility and caring for their infants.
highlights: Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week
Leave may be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously

sections.About this support:
SPL (2013)
SPL (from 1 Apr 2025)
**Amount of leave entitled**
Eligible working fathers can take up to 4 weeks of leave from their wife’s Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) or Adoption Leave (AL).
Child’s birth or estimated delivery date or Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date:
- If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, up to 6 weeks of leave to be shared between parents
- If on or after 1 Apr 2026, up to 10 weeks of leave to be shared between parents
**Amount of government reimbursement/payment**
Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000 for 4 weeks.
Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week.
**Flexibility of leave**
Flexibility for leave to be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously, with mutual agreement between employer and employee.
**When can SPL be taken?**
Within 12 months from the child's date of birth.
- After Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML)/ Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL)/ Adoption Leave (AL) is fully consumed; and
- Within 12 months from the child’s date of birth.
sections.Who is this for?:
Parents whose child is born, or has an estimated delivery date (EDD), or formal intent to adopt (FIA) date **on or after 1 Apr 2025**, are entitled to the [new SPL scheme](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave) and should not be making an election for 2013-SPL.

SPL (2013) (For father)
SPL (from 1 Apr 2025) (For both father and mother)
**For live births**
- Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth
- Child's birth or estimated delivery date is between 1 Jul 2017 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)
- Wife is eligible for Government-Paid Maternity Leave or Adoption Leave and agrees to share the leave
- Married to child's mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth
- Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth
- Child’s birth or estimated delivery date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks of SPL
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks of SPL
- For fathers: Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth
- For employee: Served employer for at least 3 months before child’s birth
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before child’s birth
**For stillbirths**
- The date of stillbirth is between 1 Nov 2021 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)
- Either you or the child’s mother are Singapore citizens
NIL
**For adoptive child**
- Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date between 1 Jul 2017 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)
- Married to the adoptive mother when the election for 2013-SPL was made
- If child is not Singapore citizen (SC), either you or the adoptive mother has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance
- Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks of SPL
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks of SPL
- Not the natural father or mother of child
- If child is not Singapore citizen (SC), either adoptive mother or father of child has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance
- For employee: Served employer for at least 3 months before FIA date
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before FIA date
sections.How to apply?:
**For SPL (2013)**

- Discuss and agree on the leave arrangement with your wife.

- Your wife must declare her intention to share her leave through the [Share My Leave eService](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/share-my-leave) in the Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal no earlier than 16 weeks before your child’s estimated delivery date.

**For employees:**
Notify your employer of the leave arrangement and submit the [declaration form (SPL1)](https://go.gov.sg/spl1form) with necessary documents.
**For self-employed:**
Record your SPL dates and submit your claim online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the last date of your SPL.
**For employers:**
- Obtain and verify the [declaration form (SPL1)](https://go.gov.sg/spl1form) and supporting documents from your employee.
- Keep the declaration form or records for 5 years from the last leave date for audit purposes.
- Verify that your employee’s wife has made a declaration to share her leave in the Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal. Check all supporting documents to confirm your employee’s eligibility.
Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) no later than 3 months after the last date of your employee’s SPL.

**For SPL (from 1 Apr 2025)**

Please refer to details on the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave/).

description: Quarterly rebates to offset HDB households’ utilities expenses. In FY2026, eligible households will receive up to $760 in U-Save rebates.
highlights: Up to $190 of additional U-Save rebates (Oct 2026 and Jan 2027) for eligible HDB households
Total of $440 to $760 in U-Save rebates for eligible HDB households in FY2026
No application needed

sections.About this support:
**2026 Additional U-Save**

- $110 to $190 for eligible HDB households on top of GSTV – U-Save in October 2026 and January 2027
- Will be credited to eligible households at the same time as the GSTV – U-Save, in October 2026 and January 2027

**GST Voucher (GSTV) – U-Save**

- $220 to $380 in GSTV – U-Save for eligible HDB households
- Will be credited in April, July, October 2026, and January 2027

**Budget 2026 U-Save**

- $110 to $190 for eligible HDB households on top of GSTV – U-Save, which helps households with utilities expenses, cushioning the impact of higher utility bills due to an increase in carbon tax from 2026

sections.Who is this for?:
- Singaporean households living in HDB flats
- If the HDB flat is partially rented out or not rented out, there must be at least 1 Singapore Citizen owner or occupier in the household
- If the entire HDB flat is rented out, there must be at least 1 Singapore Citizen tenant

title: Government-Paid Childcare Leave (GPCL) and Extended Childcare Leave (ECL)
description: Provides up to 6 days of leave for eligible working parents and legal guardians with children below 7 years old, and 2 days for those with children aged 7 to 12.
highlights: Up to 6 days of Government-Paid Childcare Leave (GPCL) for parents with a Singapore citizen child below 7 years old, capped at $500 per day for the 4th to 6th day, up to $1,500 per year
2 days of Extended Childcare Leave (ECL) for parents with a Singapore citizen child aged 7 to 12, capped at $500 per day, up to $1,000 per year

sections.About this support:
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Childcare Leave and Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

**For parents with a Singapore citizen child below 7 years old**:

- Up to 6 days of Government-Paid Childcare Leave (GPCL)
- Employer pays for the first 3 days of GPCL
- Government reimburses for the 4th to 6th day, capped at $500 per day, up to $1,500 per year

**For parents with a Singapore citizen child between 7 and 12 years old:**

- 2 days of Extended Childcare Leave (ECL)
- Fully reimbursed by the Government, capped at $500 per day, up to $1,000 per year.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen child below 7 years old for GPCL or obtains Singapore citizenship within the calendar year
- Singapore Citizen child aged 7 to 12 years old for ECL or obtains Singapore citizenship within the calendar year
- Parent has served employer for at least 3 months or been self-employed for at least 3 months and have lost income from ceasing to be actively engaged during your GPCL/ECL period.
- Adoptive parents, eligible only after Adoption Order is passed
- Natural fathers not eligible if not lawfully married to the child's mother at conception and not married subsequently
- Foster parents eligible until they cease providing care, protection or supervision
- Legal guardians with court-appointed guardianship eligible
sections.How to apply?:
**For employees:**

- Inform your employer of your leave plans.
- For foster parents, show your Letter of Identity to your employer as proof that a foster child has been placed under your care under the Children and Young Persons Act. Your employer can write in to the MSF Fostering Service at fostering@msf.gov.sg to verify your eligibility for GPCL/ECL
- For legal guardians, provide a copy of your Legal Guardianship document (i.e. Order of Court) to your employer, for verification on your GPCL/ECL eligibility.
- Submit a [declaration form (GPCL1)](https://go.gov.sg/gpcl1form) with necessary documents.
- Apply for leave as per your employer's procedures.

**For self-employed:**

- Record your leave dates.
- Submit your claim on the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the calendar year ends.

**For employers:**

- Collect and verify the [declaration form (GPCL1)](https://go.gov.sg/gpcl1form) from your employee.
- Submit your reimbursement claim on the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the 12-month period ends.

title: Adoption Leave for Mothers (AL)
description: Provides up to 12 weeks of leave for eligible adoptive mothers to care for their adopted child.
highlights: Up to 12 weeks of Adoption Leave for eligible adoptive mothers
Government reimbursement capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 for the first and second child orders
For the third and subsequent child orders, the government will reimburse up to $30,000

sections.About this support:
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

- Up to 12 weeks of Adoption Leave (AL) for mothers to care for their adopted infant.
- For the first and second child, the employer pays for the first 4 weeks; the government reimburses the 5th to 12th week, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 per child order.
- For the third and subsequent child, the government reimburses all 12 weeks, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $30,000 per child order.
- Option to share up to 4 weeks of Adoption Leave (AL) with the adoptive father under the Government-Paid Shared Parental Leave scheme.
sections.Who is this for?:
- You are not the natural mother of the child
- Adopting a child in accordance with any Singapore law relating to the adopting of children.
- Child is below 12 months old on your Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date
- FIA date on or after 1 July 2017
- You are employed or self-employed for at least 3 months before FIA date
- If child is not a Singapore citizen on adoption application date, he/she must have a Dependent's Pass (DP) and either parent must have been a Singapore citizen since the issue date
sections.How to apply?:

sections.Who is this for?:
- At least 1 applicant must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- The core member(s)* in the HFE letter application must not have previously taken 2 or more housing loans from HDB
- Singles aged 35 and above who are buying a 2-room Flexi flat on 99-year lease from HDB or a 5-room or smaller resale flat
- Senior citizens aged 55 and above who are not applying for a 2-room Flexi flat on a short lease or a Community Care Apartment (CCA)
- Your average gross monthly household income must not exceed:
  - $16,000 for families
  - $24,000 for extended families
  - $8,000 for singles buying under the Single Singapore Citizen (SSC) Scheme
- All persons listed in the application:
  - Cannot own or have an interest in any private residential property, local or overseas
  - Must not have disposed of any private residential property in the last 30 months before the application for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter

*Core member(s) refer to the applicant(s) and occupier(s) in an HFE letter application who enable the applicant(s) to qualify for a flat purchase under an eligibility scheme. All core members must remain in the flat application, and physically occupy the flat during the minimum occupation period (MOP) after the flat purchase. Their names cannot be removed.

**Second HDB housing loan**
You must also meet the following additional requirements:

At Point of Flat Purchase
Conditions to Take a Second HDB Housing Loan
You have disposed of the existing flat or private residential property and do not own any HDB flat
You and the essential occupier have to use up to 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the last-owned HDB flat or from private residential property disposed of at least 30 months prior to the HFE letter application.

You may retain up to $20,000 in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) and use the remaining balance to buy the flat.
You are buying a HDB flat **before** disposing of the existing one
You will be charged the commercial interest rate (pegged to the average non-promotional interest rate for HDB flats offered by the 3 local Financial Institutions (FIs)†) for the housing loan to buy the next flat.

The interest rate will be converted to the concessionary rate after you have disposed of the existing flat and used the CPF refund and up to 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal to reduce the housing loan amount for the next flat. From the CPF monies refunded, you may retain up to $20,000 in your CPF OA.

†The 3 local FIs are DBS Bank Limited, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited, and United Overseas Bank Limited.

Please note that your second HDB housing loan amount will be reduced by the full CPF refund and part of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the following residential properties:

- Existing or last-owned HDB flat
- Last-owned private residential property, disposed of at least 30 months prior to the HFE letter application

The manner of disposal includes the sale, transfer or surrender of a flat or private residential property, or by any other method under the Housing and Development Act or any other written law.

You may read more on how the cash proceeds from the disposal are used on [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb).
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HFE letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- The HFE letter will inform you of your eligibility for purchasing a flat and the amount of housing loan and grants you can receive

- Counselling and therapy sessions can be conducted in-person or online via Zoom.

**Helplines:**

- Care Corner Counselling Centre also runs a toll-free Mandarin Counselling Hotline at 1800 353 5800 daily from 10am to 10pm, excluding public holidays.
- SAMH Insight Centre also provides a toll-free helpline at 1800 287 7019 (9am to 6pm on weekdays, except 1pm to 2pm and public holidays).
sections.Who is this for?:
Individuals, couples and families with issues such as:

- Marital and relationship issues
- Family and parenting issues
- Grief and loss
- Mental health
- Personal challenges
- Stress
- Trauma
sections.How to apply?: For enquiries or appointment booking, call or email the respective service provider.
sections.What to expect?:
- The service provider will assess the request for counselling and ask your presenting issues and preferred day/time for the counselling and arrange a slot for you accordingly.
- The staff will also provide information on the fees.
- Counselling intake and assessment is conducted at the first appointment and the client will see the same counsellor for the subsequent sessions until the case is closed or transferred.
- If counselling is not suitable, the counsellor may refer you to other appropriate services.
- A counselling session takes around 1 hour.
- Most issues will need more than 1 counselling session to resolve.
- Fees payable for all service providers except SAMH Insight Centre.

title: Counselling (Seniors)
description: Provides counselling to older persons aged 50 and above and/or their caregivers, to improve their mental well-being and resilience to cope with life’s challenges.

sections.About this support:
- Gerontological counselling provides an avenue for seniors and their caregivers to discuss their issues and concerns and help to address their personal, social or psychological challenges.
- Individual and group counselling available.
- Counselling can be provided at the counselling centre or at their own home if necessary.
sections.Who is this for?:
Persons aged 50 years old and above with issues and concerns such as:

- Grief and loss
- Loneliness/isolation
- Depression
- Stress and anxiety
- Relationship problems
- Difficulty adjusting to transitions and changes (e.g. retirement, ‘empty nest’ syndrome, onset of illnesses)

Family members/caregivers who experience stress caring for their elderly loved ones who are experiencing the above-mentioned concerns can also be supported.

Hua Mei Centre for Successful Ageing also provides individual and group coaching in emotion management, inter-generational relationship-building and communication skills.
sections.How to apply?: For enquiries or appointment booking, call or email the respective service provider.
sections.What to expect?:
- The counselling centre will arrange an appointment for you with a professional counsellor who will assess your needs and advise if counselling is able to meet your needs.
- If counselling is not suitable, the counsellor will refer you to other appropriate services.
- A counselling session takes around 1 to 1.5 hours.
- Most issues will need more than 1 counselling session to resolve.
- Fees payable for Hua Mei Centre for Successful Ageing and O’Joy Limited.

title: Life! Mentors
description: A 5-8 year mentoring programme that supports children (6-13 years old) a fair chance to succeed in life.

sections.About this support:
The programme core services includes

- 1-1 mentoring
- Group mentoring
- Family bonding activities
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore citizens/ Singapore PRs aged 6 – 13 years old from vulnerable backgrounds (e.g. ComLink+ families, parental incarceration, referral from school counsellors).
sections.How to apply?: Walk in to any of  Life Community Services Society centres or referral by school counsellors or fill in the online contact form (https://life-community.org/contact-us/)
sections.What to expect?: Programme staff will conduct intake and needs assessment within one month of the referral. For higher needs and urgent cases, it will be conducted within two weeks. Programme staff will contact the caregiver via phone call or text messages to introduce the programme, share the online intake form, and arrange a home visit.

title: Caregivers Training Grant (CTG)
description: Subsidy for caregivers to offset the training fees of approved courses to equip themselves with the necessary skills to care for their loved ones.
highlights: $400 subsidy for the first year
$200 annual top-up, with a total CTG balance cap of $400 at any given time
Contact the service provider at least two weeks before the course starts

sections.About this support:
- $400 grant for eligible care recipients in their first year of tapping on CTG
- CTG balance can be used to subsidise their caregivers attending approved caregiver training courses
- Co-payment of at least $10 for every course attended by the caregiver
- $200 annual top-up in subsequent years, with total CTG balance capped at $400 at any given time
- If multiple caregivers of the same care recipient wish to attend training, they can tap on the same CTG balance available to offset the course fees
sections.Who is this for?:
Care recipient must be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 65 and older

OR

- Have a disability assessed by an approved healthcare practitioner

Caregiver must be:

- Main person caring for the care recipient (e.g. family members and foreign domestic workers)
sections.How to apply?:
- [Choose an approved course here](https://training-healthcare.vertis.digital/)
- Contact the training provider to confirm course details
- Register for the course
- Inform the trainer about using CTG at least two weeks before the course starts
- Your trainer will give you the CTG application form to fill out, and will submit it on your behalf
- [You can also visit the AIC’s website to download the CTG application form](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Caregivers-Training-Grant)
sections.Where to go: [Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)
sections.Phone number:
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

title: Child LifeSG Credits
description: Provides broad-based support for Singaporean families with children.
highlights: $500 Child LifeSG Credits for every Singapore Citizen child aged 0 to 12
Disbursed to eligible child's CDA trustee via the LifeSG mobile app
Can be used to defray household expenses

sections.About this support:
- $500 Child LifeSG Credits disbursed to the Child Development Account (CDA) trustee of the child via the LifeSG mobile app
- Can be used at merchants that accept payments using PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR
- Credits are valid for 12 months from disbursement, with the expiry date displayed in the LifeSG mobile app

sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen
- 2025 Child LifeSG Credits: Aged 0 to 12 in 2025 (born from 1 January 2013 to 31 December 2025)
- 2026 Child LifeSG Credits: Aged 0 to 12 in 2026 (born from 1 January 2014 to 31 December 2026)

- [View more details](https://ask.gov.sg/msf?topic=Child LifeSG Credits)

sections.Phone number: Baby Bonus and Large Families Scheme hotline: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222)

title: Experiential Learning and Mentoring Programme (ELMP)
description: Supports youths through mentoring and, experiential learning. It provides youths with a safe and conducive place to hang out after school and empowers them with pro-social skills and resilience.

sections.About this support:
The programme engages youth through:

- Centre-based drop-in activities like tchoukball training and small group tuitions
- Experiential learning activities and workshops
- 1 to 1 mentoring sessions with mentors

The activities are conducted once a week.
sections.Who is this for?: Youths aged 11 to 19 years old who are enrolled in school social work programmes, as well as those referred from school counsellors and parents.
sections.How to apply?: Youths or their parents can approach or call the centre directly.
sections.What to expect?:
- An intake assessment will be conducted.
- Youths will be matched to a suitable mentor thereafter.

title: The Builders Project
description: Aims to increase social capital and social discipline, and accomplish positive outcomes in Primary 4-6 school children who have been assessed to have higher needs.

sections.About this support: The Builders Project is an early intervention programme targeting Primary 4-5 school children that aims to promote positive school climate and culture that are conducive for achieving social capital and social discipline. The programme works with the parents and teachers of the identified students which leads to better school outcomes such as lower chronic school absenteeism, premature withdrawal from school and other adolescent risk behaviours.
sections.Who is this for?:
P4 to P6 children who:

- Are in mainstream primary schools
- Have been assessed to have higher need
sections.How to apply?: - Schools will refer students to the programme.
sections.What to expect?:
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools.
- Lutheran Community Care Services (LCCS) will administer a pre-screening tool to students referred by teachers and social workers.
- Based on the results, LCCS and teachers will jointly decide on the identified students who are suitable for further support.

title: MightyKids, Families & Community (MightyKFC)
description: MightyKFC is a developmental mentoring programme that aims to nurture at-risk children and youth in the Telok Blangah region.

sections.About this support:
MightyKFC is a developmental mentoring programme with the following service components:

- Centre based activities
- Life skills workshops
- Individual mentoring
- Community service
- Parent-child bonding session
sections.Who is this for?:
- MightyKFC’s client group is latchkey children and youth from the lower income group, aged 4 – 16 years old.
- MightyKFC targets children and youth who primarily reside or study in schools in the Telok Blangah region.
sections.How to apply?:
You may:

- Walk into the centre
- Email to [mkfc@life-community.org](mailto:mkfc@life-community.org)
- Call the centre at [62707198](tel:62707198)
sections.What to expect?:
- An intake interview will be arranged to register for the programme.
- Upon successful registration, services will be provided to the service users for the duration of the programme at the activity centre.

title: Halogen SPARK!
description: A structured evidence-based entrepreneurship curriculum that targets Secondary 3 students who are from the G1/G2 Subject Based Banding (SBB) Stream that improves better school-focused outcomes, including their attendance and academic performance.

sections.About this support:
Halogen SPARK! is an upstream intervention programme that targets Secondary students who are from the G1/G2 SBB stream. It targets pre/low/mid-risk students from the Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) and/or come from challenging and disadvantaged backgrounds.

The programme is a structured evidence-based programme developed by NFTE (Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship), where the key objectives are to increase service users' social-emotional and academic competencies through the incorporation of English and Math in the programme curriculum. It supports the development of numeracy and literacy skills through the entrepreneurship modules, and aims to instill self-confidence and self-efficacy in youths.
sections.Who is this for?: Secondary 3 students who are from the G1/G2 Subject Based Banding (SBB) stream
sections.How to apply?:
- Schools will refer the students to the programme at the start of the calendar year.
- Halogen SPARK! and teachers will jointly decide on the identified students on their service eligibility.
sections.What to expect?:
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools.
- Halogen SPARK! will conduct a pre-programme survey for all enrolled students for the purpose of further adjustments to the programmes depending on the student demographics.

title: Live On!
description: Year-long, family-centric psychological intervention for youths with high suicide risk as they transit from hospitalisation into the community.

sections.About this support:
- LiveOn! is a 1-year high frequency and intensive suicide intervention programme that targets youths aged 12 to 18 years old with suicidality risk, and includes their family members in the intervention.
- Objectives of the programme includes:
  - Providing immediate support to youths with suicidal thoughts or attempts in the community
  - Providing continuous community support for youths and the families once they are discharged from primary care institutions
  - De-escalating youths' emotions and strengthening family support through individual and family counselling
sections.Who is this for?: - 12 to 18 years old youths who have been discharged from IMH due to suicidality.
sections.How to apply?:
- This programme is only eligible for youths who have been discharged by IMH, KKH, NUH, and other public hospitals due to suicidality, and have been assessed by a clinician to be eligible for referral.
- Call the TOUCHline (1800 377 2252, 9am to 6pm from Monday to Friday) or email [mentalhealth@touch.org.sg](mailto:mentalhealth@touch.org.sg) if you do not have a hospital referral but still require support.
- If you are suicidal and require immediate support, call Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) at 1767.
sections.What to expect?:
This programme consists of individual counselling for the youths, as well as family sessions.

**Individual sessions (for the youth)**

- In the Acute phase, the youth will meet with the social worker / counsellor / psychologist weekly for 6 to 12 sessions to de-escalate emotions.
- In the Continuation phase, the youth will meet with the social worker / counsellor / psychologist twice a month, for another 5 to 12 sessions.
- In the Maintenance phase after the above is completed, the youth will remain in contact with the caseworker through calls and text messages for 3 to 6 months for continuous support and monitoring . If youths relapse, an assessment will be conducted and the case will be re-opened.

**Family sessions (for the caregivers of the youth)**

- Meet with the social worker / counsellor twice a month from the start of the programme for 4 to 6 sessions to learn skills on how to support the youth better, which includes safety planning and crisis management School counsellors will also be contacted, with client and parental consent.

title: Safe Place
description: Programme aims to empower women and their families with unsupported pregnancies to make informed and life-giving choices.

sections.About this support:
The programme provides the following services:

- Case management and counselling
- Pre- and postnatal skills equipping
- Baby essentials
- Temporary accommodation
- Referrals to other support partners
sections.Who is this for?: Safe Place serves pregnant women up to 32 weeks gestation who consent to receiving support services. For clients under 17 years, parental consent is required, although exceptions are considered based on individual circumstances.
sections.How to apply?:
If you are a pregnant woman who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about unsupported pregnancy, please contact Safe Place at 6817 4202 or text via WhatsApp at 8891 4214 to speak to the caseworkers.

For community partners, please submit a referral form and attach a social report (if available) via email ([safeplace@lakeside.org.sg](mailto:safeplace@lakeside.org.sg)).

A social worker will be in touch within 3 working days.
sections.What to expect?:
Service users who require help with their pregnancy may contact Safe Place via email/call/WhatsApp.

Case plans and duration of case are customised to meet the unique needs and circumstances of the service users.

title: Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS)
description: Provides temporary housing for families as they await the completion of their new flats.
highlights: Rent a flat from HDB while waiting for your uncompleted HDB flat
Subsidised rental rates range between $400 to $1,500 for 2-, 3- or 4-room flats
Eligible households may submit applications online

sections.About this support:
- To rent a flat from HDB at a subsidised rate while waiting for your flat to be completed
- Rental rates depend on the location and flat type, and can range from $400 to $1,500 per month
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen who is with another Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident in the PPHS household
- Booked an uncompleted flat under HDB's sales exercises as a married couple, under the Fiance/Fiancee scheme, or as a divorced or widowed parent with children
- All members of the PPHS household must not own an existing HDB flat
- Monthly household income of less than or equal to $8,000
sections.How to apply?: You can apply online at the [HDB website](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/renting-a-flat/parenthood-provisional-housing-scheme/application-process). PPHS application window will be from the 1st to the 14th of even months (Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, Dec).

title: Sober Living Framework (SLF)
description: Provides crisis intervention, therapy support, and long-term aftercare for persons and families impacted by substance and/or behavioural addictions.

sections.About this support:
The SLF comprises intervention tracks for addicted persons or Significant Other Persons (SOP; includes kin and family members, partner, close friends, guardian) at 5 different stages of needs:

- Track 1: Outreach, Education and Awareness – to raise awareness of addictions and advocate for early intervention
- Track 2: Relapse Prevention and Extended Care – individual and group counselling, family support, self-help support group
- Track 3: Sober Living – for persons in the early remission phase with less than 6 months sobriety from addictive behaviour
- Track 4: Maintenance – for persons with at least 6 months sobriety
- Track 5: For Family/SOP – individual and group counselling, support group

Note: Not all participants will enter and complete each track in a linear order.
sections.Who is this for?:
All services are open to Singapore Citizens and persons residing in Singapore who are:

- Assessed to have a present or past addiction issue (including drugs, alcohol, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, sex, porn use and gaming), with the expressed desire to seek help or,
- Currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

For addiction treatment:

- Services are provided to all persons aged 14 and above

For family counselling:

- Support is provided to individuals aged 10 and above

For outreach programmes:

- Conducted for individuals aged 14 and above

Those who are under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a parent, guardian or authorised adult.
sections.How to apply?: You may contact WE CARE for more information. Alternatively, WE CARE also accepts referrals through other agencies (e.g. State Courts, MSF, Prisons, family service centres, hospitals, other social service agencies).
sections.What to expect?:
The intake and assessment process involves an interview where the person’s motivation is assessed and their readiness, reasons and desire for change are explored.

- For persons who are assessed to be ambivalent about stopping their addictive behaviour, brief therapy will be conducted, with the primary goal of engaging with the person such that they will return for help in the future when ready for change.
- For persons who are assessed to be highly motivated for change, they will be recommended to seek medical detoxification (if necessary), or directly assigned to the relevant track.

title: Maintenance Support Central (MSC)
description: Provides support and assistance for clients who have difficulty in receiving spousal and/or child maintenance.

sections.About this support:
MSC empowers individuals by providing knowledge of their marital and maintenance rights while offering comprehensive support in collaboration with community partners.

1.      Maintenance Applications

- Assists in the filing of Fresh Maintenance Applications (FMO) via the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS)
- Assists in the Enforcement of Maintenance Orders (EMO) through video-link filing (iFAMS)
- Appointments must be made in advance

2.      Legal Clinics

- Offers Civil Family Law legal clinic on the first and third Monday evenings of each month
- Offers Syariah Family Law legal clinic on the third Monday of each month
- Legal clinics are open to individuals residing in Singapore, with an income cap criteria

3.      Court Process Guidance

- Offers legal guidance which includes explanation of standard legal procedures and legal terms related to family law

4.      Counselling Services

- Provides face-to-face and phone counselling for individuals who require emotional support for marital issues, post-divorce/separations, parenthood struggles, and/or similar concerns
- Counselling services are chargeable, based on clients’ financial capabilities

5.      Educational Talks

- Legal talks on family law matters designed to benefit the public, social service professionals, and community partners. These sessions aim to raise awareness, enhance understanding, and equip participants with practical knowledge to navigate legal challenges effectively.
- Talks are conducted by guest speakers who are experts in Family and Syariah law

MSC also assists in responding to enquiries by sharing information or referring them to other community partners.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Services are rendered to individuals residing in Singapore who face financial abuse, marital issues, or have a Singapore court order and require legal support to navigate family law matters.
- This includes individuals who are dealing with unpaid maintenance, divorce proceedings, and financial difficulties arising from marital conflicts.
sections.How to apply?:
- You may apply to file Fresh or Enforcement of Maintenance application online (https://ifams.gov.sg/sop/#iFAMS). Alternatively, you may also contact the MSC programme's hotline at 6837 0611 to make an appointment.
- You can register for the online legal clinic (https://forms.office.com/r/4JucwmuQfc). If you qualify, programme staff will get back to you by 3 working days on the details.
- You may register for counselling service online (https://forms.office.com/r/mvdxTJcBFF) or call the hotline at 6571 0185 / 6837 0611 (WhatsApp)
sections.What to expect?: Service users who require the programme’s services will need to complete a registration form. Staff will confirm the appointments with the service user within 3 to 5 working days of form submission. For clients who register for legal clinic or counselling service, the processing time is 3 working days. All other services can be arranged at the time of contact.

title: HCSA SPIN
description: SPIN supports single parents and lone caregivers through casework and counselling, social support network such as befriending, practical support and an online portal of information and resources.

sections.About this support:
SPIN aims to empower single parents and lone caregivers to be resilient and self-reliant, and to help them attain increased capacity in caregiving/parenting, improve their social support, psychological well-being and increase their access to practical resources.

Services include:

- Needs assessment by social workers and co-creation of individualised care plans with single parents/lone caregivers to address identified needs.
- Counselling for single parents and children who have been assessed to be in need for emotional and mental health support.
- Befriending and peer support for single parents to build social support and trust amongst other parents and volunteers
- Counselling, tuition and homework support for the children (aged 7 to 17) of the clients
- Workshops and events to empower single parents with essential life and career skills
- Practical support such as referrals to resource channels to support clients in meeting identified needs, disbursement of grocery vouchers and food items
sections.Who is this for?:
- Single parents or lone caregivers of children below 18 years old, and these children
- No income criteria and no geographical boundaries
sections.How to apply?:
You may

1. Approach any Family Service Centre (FSC) for referral, or
2. Sign up online at https://crm.hcsa.org.sg/spin-member-application-form/ to fill up the online registration form, or
3. Call or email the programme for assistance in signing up.
sections.What to expect?: A social work associate will respond to the enquiry/referral within 3-5 working days and arrange for intake assessment. Thereafter, a social worker will be assigned to the parent, and trained befrienders will be matched to the parent. The programme is for a maximum period of 12 months. After the programme ends, the parent will be invited to join the Alumni Chapter to continue staying connected with a community and contribute to a supportive network of single-parent families.

title: Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA)
description: Provides educational financial support for eligible Singapore Citizens' post-secondary education.
highlights: Funds can be used for approved programmes, repay government loans, and financial schemes
No application needed

sections.About this support:
- PSEA Funds can be used to pay:
  - one's own or siblings’ approved education programmes at approved institutions
  - government education loans and financial schemes
- PSEA balances earn interest at the same rate as the CPF Ordinary Account (CPF-OA), currently 2.5% per annum
- Unused PSEA funds will be transferred to the CPF-OA when the account holder turns 31, subject to CPF-OA usage rules
sections.Who is this for?:
- You must be a Singapore Citizen with a balance in either:
  - the Child Development Account (CDA) when it is closed
  - the Edusave Account when turning 17 years old or is no longer studying in a Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded school, whichever is later
- The PSEA will also be opened for Singapore Citizens who are:
  - eligible for PSEA top-ups by the Government
  - recipient of the first payment of the National Service Housing, Medical and Education (NS HOME) Awards
  - recipient of the annual education bursary under the Home Ownership Plus Education (HOPE) Scheme
sections.How to apply?: No application required.
sections.Where to go:
[MOE Customer Service Centre, 1 North Buona Vista Drive MOE Building, Podium Block Singapore 138675](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)

Note: By appointment only.

title: Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML)
description: Provides up to 16 weeks of paid leave for eligible working mothers to care for their newborns.
highlights: Up to 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) for eligible working mothers
For the first and second child, the employer pays for the first 8 weeks, and the government reimburses the 9th to 16th week, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000
For the third and subsequent child, the government reimburses all 16 weeks, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $40,000

sections.About this support:
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

- Up to 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) for eligible working mothers.
- For the first and second child, the employer pays for the first 8 weeks, and the government reimburses the 9th to 16th week, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 per child order.
- For the third and subsequent child, the government reimburses all 16 weeks, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $40,000 per child order.
- Option to share up to 4 weeks of GPML with the spouse under the Government-Paid Shared Parental Leave scheme.
sections.Who is this for?:
**For live births**:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Child is a Singapore Citizen at birth or within 12 months after birth
- For employees: Served employer for at least 3 months before child's birth (GPML that is granted despite not meeting this criterion **cannot be shared** with your husband under the SPL scheme)
- For self-employed: Engaged in work for at least 3 months before child's birth and lost income during maternity leave

**For stillbirths**: 
Similar conditions apply, with additional criteria:

- The date of stillbirth is on or after 1 November 2021
- You are a Singapore Citizen at the time of stillbirth or the child’s father is a Singapore Citizen and was lawfully married to the mother at some point between conception and stillbirth
sections.How to apply?:
**For employees**:

- Notify your employer at least one week before starting maternity leave.
- Submit the [declaration form (GPML1)](https://file.go.gov.sg/gpml1form.pdf) to your employer with necessary documents at least one week before starting your Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML), or within one month from your child’s birth.
- Follow your employer’s leave application process.

**For self-employed**:

- Keep a record of your GPML dates
- Submit your claim online via the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) after starting the government-paid portion of your GPML
- Claims should be made within three months after the last day of your GPML

**For employers**:

- Obtain and verify the declaration form (GPML1) from your employee
- Keep the declaration form or records for five years from the last GPML date
- Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) after your employee has taken the government-paid portion of GPML
- Claims should be made within three months after the last day of the employee’s GPML
sections.Phone number:
MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222) 
(say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

title: CARENIGHTS
description: Supports children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families with structured evening care services.

sections.About this support: The CareNights programme is a structured evening care for children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families, including those referred through ComLink+ or other community partners. It addresses a critical gap in after-school support, particularly helping caregivers who are working, attending training, or managing caregiving responsibilities.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Caregivers with children aged 6 to 14 and are experiencing caregiving challenges
- Low income (gross household income not exceeding $4,500 per month or per capita income not exceeding $1,125 per month) and/or ComLink+ families
- Families coping with extenuating circumstances beyond those described above will be admitted on a case-by-case basis
sections.How to apply?:
- Referral through schools, social service agencies, and government agencies
- Submission of enquiries through Morning Star Community Services' Website
sections.What to expect?:
- Structured evening care
- The agency provide safe and nuturing environment during evening hours.
- The agency aims to strengthen parent-child through facilited bonding activities and workshops.

title: Babes Pregnancy Crisis Support
description: For individuals aged 21 and below needing support with their pregnancy, so that they are aware of their options and are able to make an informed decision regarding their pregnancy.

sections.About this support:
Babes supports pregnant teens through:

- Casework and counselling
- 24-hour helpline
- Practical support (befriender, baby essentials, employment & back to school assistance etc)
- Information & resources
- Outreach and youth engagement events
sections.Who is this for?:
- Pregnant teenager who needs help; Anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
sections.How to apply?: If you are a pregnant teen who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about teenage pregnancy, please contact Babes' 24-hour helpline at 6206 6641 or text via WhatsApp at 8111 3535 to speak to the caseworkers.
sections.What to expect?:
- Teenagers who require help with their pregnancy and/or anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy may contact Babes via the 24-hour helpline (call/text).
- When an enquiry is attended to, the Helpliner will also assess if the teenager is eligible to be a case under Babes. Should the assessment be one that Babes can assist, Babes will arrange for a meeting with the teenager and/or her family/partner within 3-5 working days to assess the needs and provide the necessary support and guidance.

title: MUIS Zakat Financial Assistance
description: Provides monthly financial assistance and support in other forms to eligible low-income Muslim households.
highlights: Monthly financial assistance for eligible individuals
Support for emergency needs and burial expenses
Study grants and food vouchers available
Assessment based on Per Capita Income of $500 or lower for eligibility

sections.About this support:
Potential benefits include:

- Monthly financial support: Dependent on Per Capita Income (PCI) criteria

  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks

  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks

- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before child’s birth

sections.Who is this for?:
Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above*^#
- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye

  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)
sections.How to apply?:
- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).
- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.

**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**

2. **Hardcopy submission**

  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)
  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)
  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)

title: MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) Scheme
description: Loan scheme to help students who are taking MOE-subsidised diploma, undergraduate or postgraduate programmes in publicly-funded post-secondary education institutions to finance their tuition fees and borrow a living allowance loan for other education-related expenses. It also helps undergraduates to finance cost of institution-approved overseas student programme.
highlights: Base provision and means-tested balance fee coverage components under the HESL scheme can cover up to 100% of subsidised tuition fees for eligible Singapore Citizen (SC) students
Eligible students who meet the income eligibility criteria can also apply for a living allowance loan component under the HESL scheme to cover their education expenses
Loan is interest-free during the course of study; interest and repayment commence upon a student’s graduation or leaving the institution

sections.About this support:
For Diploma students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
·  Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC only)
·  Living allowance loan of up to $3,200 per academic year
For Undergraduate and Postgraduate students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
· Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC undergraduates only)
· Living allowance loan of up to $4,100 per academic year (for full-time undergraduate students only)
· Loan to cover up to $12,000 for the cost of one institution-approved overseas student programme (for full-time SC undergraduates only)
sections.Who is this for?:
The HESL will be available to the following students, and the loan components available will depend on the student’s citizenship and level of study:

- SC, Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) and international student (IS) studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in any of the local polytechnics.
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in Institute of Technical Education (ITE).
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma and undergraduate programmes in LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE), Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and University of the Arts Singapore (UAS).
- SC, PR and IS studying full-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate, full-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by coursework, and full-time/part-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by research programmes in autonomous universities.
- SC studying part-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate programmes in autonomous universities.

Depending on the level of study and type of institution, the means-tested loan provisions are for:

- SC and PR with gross monthly household per capita income (PCI)^ of $3,500 or less.
- IS with gross monthly household PCI of $1,875 or less.

sections.Who is this for?:
- Child is a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident (at least one immediate family member in the same household must be a Singapore Citizen)
- Both you and your spouse are each working at least 56 hours a month
- Child must attend a Student Care Centre registered with MSF
- For children attending SCCs aged 7 to 14 years old (Primary 1 to Secondary 2) in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $4,500 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $1,125 or less for families with 5 or more members. From January 2027: The monthly gross household income must be $6,500 or less, or monthly household income per capita must be $1,625 or less.
  For children attending SSCCs aged 7 to 18 years old in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $9,200 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $2,300 or less for families with 5 more members. Please visit [Enabling Guide by SG Enable](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/special-student-care-centres) for more information on the subsidies.

**How Income is Calculated**

- For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income over 12 months from CPF records or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years).
Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
- For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years), or income declared to CPF Board.

**Note:** Family members refer to the child’s grandparents or siblings below 21 years old who live at the same address, are not working or have no income, and are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

Your gross monthly income will be determined via HOMES as part of the means-test.

For further information, please refer to [MSF | Student Care Fee Assistance](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/student-care/for-parents/student-care-fee-assistance).
sections.How to apply?:
All SCFA applications must be submitted online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/scfa)  at least six months before the intended start date. For example, if you wish to apply for SCFA effective from January 2027, you may submit the application from July 2026 onwards. SCFA approval will commence from the month in which the application is received, or from the month following the expiry of any existing SCFA, whichever is later.

[Click here to learn more about the SCFA application process.](https://www.msf.gov.sg/docs/default-source/student-care/scfa-infographic---application-process.pdf)

- If you're unemployed or looking for work, you will need to provide supporting documents (for example, proof of job search, medical letter, or medical certificate).
- With the SCFA, if you still face difficulties with the monthly co-payment of your child's student care fees, you may submit an appeal through the SCC, along with supporting documents detailing the change in circumstances and an explanation of the reasons for the appeal. Appeals will be considered on a case-by-case basis, and if approved, will commence from the month when the appeal was submitted

title: Early Intervention Programme for Infants & Children (EIPIC)
description: EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0-6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

sections.About this support:
EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0 to 6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

The continuum of EI services include:

- EIPIC Under-2s
  - Targeted at children under 2 years old
  - Trains parents/caregivers so that they can effectively carry out intervention strategies in the child’s daily routines at home
- EIPIC@Centre
  - Provides both therapy and educational intervention services, typically in small groups
- DS-Plus
  - Provided in preschools targeted at children aged 2 to 6 years requiring low levels of EI support, and are attending preschools.
sections.Who is this for?:
Children who are:

- From birth to 6 years old
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents;
- Assessed by a paediatrician to be at risk of a developmental, intellectual, sensory or physical disability, or a combination of disabilities; and
- Not concurrently enrolled in any other ECDA-funded EI programmes (i.e. DS-LS, DS-Plus programmes).
sections.How to apply?:
- You may approach a doctor at any polyclinic to obtain referral for assessment at the Department of Child Development (DCD) at KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) or Child Development Unit (CDU) at National University Hospital (NUH).
- Alternatively, you may approach a private paediatrician for assessment and recommendation for EIPIC.
- If your child is assessed to be suitable for EIPIC, the hospital or the private paediatrician will recommend EIPIC and submit the application to SG Enable upon your consent.

More information can be found on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/therapy-intervention/early-intervention-programme-for-infants-children).
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days to provide necessary information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of EI Centre.
- Your selected EI Centre will contact you within 2 weeks of referral to arrange an interview and assessment of your child.
- Enrolment into a suitable programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies at the centre and approval of the respective centre management.
