- Applicants must be Singapore Citizens at least 21 years old
- The household must include at least 1 other Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- All applicants and occupiers must have no ownership or interest in private property locally or overseas in the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property
- Grant amount eligibility will be [determined by your household’s average monthly household income (includes all applicants and occupiers listed in the EC application)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/executive-condominiums/cpf-housing-grant)
- All members of the core family nucleus will receive equal shares of the grant, fully credited into their CPF Ordinary Accounts
- Only core applicants can use their grants to pay for the EC unit purchase
sections.How to apply?: Contact the property developer directly for details on the application process and required documents.

title: Housing Loan from Financial Institutions (FI)
description: Supports your flat purchase through housing loans from Financial Institutions (FI) regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
highlights: Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit up to 75% of the flat’s purchase price / resale price and value
Repayment period up to 30 years

sections.About this support:
- LTV limit of up to 75% for both new and resale flats
- Repayment period of up to 30 years
- Option to use any amount in OA for flat purchase, dependent on [certain applicable limits](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-financial-institutions)
- Can refinance the housing loan with another loan from a different FI or a different interest rate package
sections.Who is this for?:
- Applicants must pay at least 5% of the flat price or flat value (whichever is lower) in cash. The minimum cash payment is dependent on applicants’ age, loan period and whether there are any outstanding housing loans
- Applicants who want to purchase a unit from a property developer under the Executive Condominium Housing Scheme must take a housing loan from an FI
- LTV limit is up to 75% of the flat purchase price or flat value, whichever is lower. FIs may have restrictions on flat purchase depending on remaining lease of the flat and / or if your repayment period exceeds 25 years or you have additional housing loan(s)
sections.How to apply?:
- [Compare housing loan packages from participating Fis](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/budget)
- Apply early for an In-Principle Approval (IPA) from participating FIs through HDB’s Integrated Loan Application service on the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp28/TimeLine/my-flat-dashboard) for an indicative assessment of your loan eligibility
- You need to obtain a valid Letter of Offer (LO) to confirm the loan offer from an FI before signing Agreement for Lease for a new flat or exercising the Option to Purchase for a resale flat
- Use the integrated loan application service on the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp28/TimeLine/my-flat-dashboard) to apply for IPA and LO)

title: Lively Places Fund
description: Provides funding of up to $20,000 for community-driven projects that enhance public spaces and foster community bonds.
highlights: Funding of up to $5,000 for small, short-term community projects
Funding of up to $20,000 for eligible larger projects
Traffic redirection support provided for street events

sections.About this support:
The funds awarded will depend on the type and scale of the project. Please refer to the below table for a detailed breakdown:

Category
Award Sum
Description
Project fund
Up to $5,000
For smaller, short-term action plans or activities for community bonding in HDB neighbourhoods

e.g. block parties, anti-littering campaign, community recycling day
Building Fund
Up to $5,000
For projects that will involve a physical transformation of existing public spaces and have an implementation period of 6 months or less

e.g. community arts projects and short-term pop-up installations to activate spaces
Up to $20,000
For projects that will involve a physical transformation of existing public spaces and have an implementation period of more than 6 months

e.g. conversion of void decks into community living rooms and cafes, longer-term pop-up installations to activate spaces
Street Closure
N/A
For short-term projects that transform streets into active public spaces for the community

Support provided will be limited to road closure essentials, consisting of safety barriers, signage and security personnel
sections.Who is this for?:
- Open to all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Individual or team applicants, with at least 1 applicant above 17 years old
- Not for projects already funded by other agencies
- Co-funding between agencies may be considered for new projects if the project meets the fund’s objectives
- Previous awardees must complete existing projects before reapplying
- Cannot support projects that duplicate existing programmes
- Does not cover projects or studies started before funding approval
- All proposals will be reviewed based on the following criteria:
  - Fund objective
  - Level of neighbourhood involvment
  - Level of community match
  - Outcomes

Refer to the [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/living-in-my-community/enlivening-my-neighbourhood/lively-places-programme/lively-places-fund-and-challenge) for more information regarding the criteria.
sections.How to apply?: Please visit https://go.gov.sg/hdb-osglpf-application

title: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Singles)
description: Provides up to $60,000 in Enhanced CPF Housing Grants (EHG) (Singles) for eligible first-timer applicants buying a new or resale flat on their own, or with their non-resident spouses.
highlights: EHG (Singles) Grant of up to $60,000 for eligible first-timer applicants
Additional up to $60,000 grant for joint singles scheme (a total of up to $120,000)
Households with lower household incomes will receive a larger grant amount

sections.About this support:
- The EHG (Singles) Grant provides up to $60,000 to offset the purchase price of the flat / reduce the required housing loan for the flat (new or resale)
- Receive a total Grant of up to $120,000 when jointly purchasing flats with other eligible first-timer single applicants (Limited to 2, up to $60,000 each)
sections.Who is this for?:
- First-timer applicants aged 35 or above, who are:
  - buying a HDB flat alone or with other first-timer single citizens
  - buying a resale flat alone, with other first-timer single citizens or with their parents
- First-timer applicants aged 21 or above who are buying a resale flat with their non-resident spouse
- If you are buying a flat with your parents, you and at least 1 parent must be a Singapore Citizen, and both parents must be first-timers and meet all the eligibility conditions
- Applicants have worked continuously for at least 12 months, 2 months before the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application, and were employed at the time of the HFE letter application
- Monthly household income not exceeding $4,500 for singles and $9,000 for joint singles, non-resident spouses or your parents (resale flats only)
- Flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- To qualify for the full EHG grant, flat must have sufficient lease for the coverage of the youngest core applicant and occupier to the age of 95
- Must not own, have an interest in or have disposed of any private residential property (local or overseas) within the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the HFE letter application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property at HFE letter application and up to 30 months before HFE letter application
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to determine your eligibility for this Grant as well as others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB
- The Grant will be credited to the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible household members
- Only core applicants can use their share of the housing grants to pay for the flat purchase

title: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Families)
description: Provides up to $120,000 for eligible first-time applicants applying as a family to assist with new or resale flat purchases.
highlights: Up to $120,000 Enhanced CPF Housing Grant for first-timer families
The Grant can be used to offset the flat purchase price or reduce the required housing loan
Households with lower household incomes will receive larger grants

sections.About this support:
- Up to $120,000 for applicants purchasing a new or resale flat as a family
- Up to $60,000 for couples comprising a first-time and second-time applicant
- The grant amount is based on the average gross monthly household income, with lower-income households receiving more support
- The Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) can be used to:
  - Offset the purchase price of the flat
  - Reduce the housing loan required for the flat purchase
sections.Who is this for?:
- Applicants forming a core family nucleus, consisting of the core applicant(s) and occupier(s)
- Average gross monthly household income of $9,000 or below for first-timer households (including all applicants and occupiers)
- For mixed households (first-timer and second-timer), half of the average gross monthly household income must not exceed $4,500
- If you are buying a flat with your parents, you and at least 1 parent must be a Singapore Citizen, and both parents must be first-timers and meet all the eligibility conditions
- Have worked continuously for at least 12 months, 2 months before the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application, and were employed at the time of the HFE letter application
- Flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- To qualify for the full grant, flat must have sufficient remaining lease to cover the youngest core applicant and/or core occupier to the age of 95
- Must not own, have an interest in or disposed of any private residential property (local or overseas) within the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the HFE application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property at HFE letter application and up to 30 months before HFE letter application
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to determine your eligibility for this Grant and others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB
- The Grant will be credited to the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible household members
- Only core applicants can use their share of the housing grants to pay for the flat purchase

title: Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme (FPPS)
description: Up to 60% of Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) and up to 40% of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats are made available for eligible first-timer buyers.
highlights: Up to 40% of BTO and 60% of SBF flats reserved for first-timer buyers
If you qualify under the FT(PMC) category, you will be eligible for FPPS
Can apply for both FPPS and 1 other priority scheme simultaneously

sections.About this support:
- Up to 40% of BTO flats and up to 60% of SBF flats are set aside for first-timer buyers
- You can apply for the FPPS priority scheme in addition to 1 other priority scheme
- A computerised ballot is conducted for each priority scheme:
  - For example, if your ballot under the Third Child Priority Scheme is not successful, your application will be balloted again under the FPPS
sections.Who is this for?:
- You and your spouse must be first-timer buyers
- Have a Singapore Citizen child (natural or legally adopted) aged 18 and below
- Expecting a child and have a doctor's certification of pregnancy
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your HFE letter application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

title: Proximity Housing Grant (Singles)
description: Provides up to $15,000 for eligible singles buying a resale flat to live with, or near, their parents or children.
highlights: Proximity Housing Grant (PHG) of $15,000 for singles living with parents or child
PHG of $10,000 for singles living near parents or child (within 4km)
If applicant is living near them, parents / child may be residing in either a HDB flat or private residential property to meet the PHG criteria

sections.About this support:
- Receive a PHG of $15,000 if living with parents or child
- Receive a PHG of $10,000 if living within 4km of parents or child
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen aged 35 or above, buying alone, with other single citizens or with their parents
- Singapore Citizen aged 21 or above, buying with a non-resident spouse
- The parents/child helping to qualify for the PHG must be Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident
- Applicants buying a resale flat to live with, or within 4km of, their parents or child
- If parents/child are living with you, they must be included in the resale flat as co-applicants or essential occupiers
- If your parents/child are living in a private residential property they do not own, it must be owner-occupied by immediate family members i.e. child, adopted child, parent(s) or parent(s)-in-law, or siblings
- The resale flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- Applicants must not have received the PHG before
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application

title: Family Care Scheme (FCS) (Proximity)
description: Helps parents and their child(ren), married or single, to live with or near each other for mutual care and support.
highlights: Parents and their child(ren), married or single, enjoy priority access when they apply for a flat to live with or near each other

sections.About this support:
- Seeks to strengthen intergenerational family support by promoting proximity living between parents and children, whether married or single.
- This scheme is also applicable to fiancé/ fiancée applicants.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Married couples, singles above 35, and seniors who wish to apply for a flat to live with or near their parents/ child(ren).
- This scheme is also applicable to fiancé/ fiancée applicants.
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your flat application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

title: Housing Subsidy - Citizen Top-Up
description: Provides a $10,000 housing subsidy for eligible Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident households when a family member becomes a Singapore Citizen.
highlights: $10,000 housing subsidy for eligible Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident households when a household member acquires Singapore citizenship
Citizen Top-Up  is credited into CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible family members
Can be used for repayment or redemption of housing loan, future HDB flat purchase or CPF withdrawal at age 55

sections.About this support:
- $10,000 housing subsidy for eligible households when a qualifying member becomes a Singapore Citizen
- The subsidy is converted into equal shares and credited fully into the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible family members
- Only core flat owners can use their share of the CPF housing grants to pay for the flat e.g. loan repayment
- The Citizen Top-Up can be used for a lump sum repayment or full redemption of an HDB housing loan
- For housing loans from financial institutions, you may additionally use it for monthly instalments
  - You must clear all outstanding housing loan arrears before you can use the grant for the above purposes
- If you have any remaining Citizen Top-Up balance and no housing loan, you may use it to buy another HDB flat in the future, or to form part of the CPF funds available for withdrawal under CPF rules at age 55
sections.Who is this for?:
- Households that have paid a $10,000 premium when buying a flat from HDB
- Households who received a reduced Family Grant for a resale flat, a Design Build and Sell Scheme flat or an Executive Condominium unit
- The Citizen Top-Up is granted when a Permanent Resident spouse, parent, child or sibling^ originally listed in the flat application obtains Singapore Citizenship, or when a Singapore Citizen child is born to the Singapore Citizen applicant and spouse originally listed in the flat application

^ For siblings, this qualification only applies to flats purchased as orphaned siblings or for families with a non-resident spouse.
sections.How to apply?:
Submit your application online:

- Use the [Application for Citizen Top-up e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg//webapp/AB22AWTopUpGrantWeb/AB22PMain#) within 6 months of meeting the citizenship criteria

title: Assistance Scheme for Second Timers (Divorced/ Widowed Parents) (ASSIST)
description: Allocates up to 5% of flats for eligible divorced or widowed parents applying for 2-room Flexi and 3-room BTO flats.
highlights: 5% of 2-room Flexi and 3-room Build-To-Order (BTO) flats allocated for eligible applicants

sections.About this support: Up to 5% of 2-room Flexi and 3-room BTO flats in non-mature estates are allocated to eligible applicants.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Divorced or widowed with at least one child (i.e. natural offspring from a legal marriage or legally adopted) aged 18 or below
- Adoptive parents must have the Adoption Order of their children when applying for a flat
- Must not have any interest in a HDB flat or private residential property after divorce / separation or spouse's demise, except for matrimonial flat / property
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your HFE letter application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

title: Tenants' Priority Scheme (TPS)
description: Allocates up to 10% of Flexi / Build-To-Order (BTO) / Sale of Balance (SBF) flats for eligible HDB rental flat tenants to help them purchase a home.
highlights: Up to 10% of 2-room Flexi and 3-room BTO / SBF flats reserved for eligible tenants

sections.About this support: Up to 10% of 2-room Flexi and 3-room BTO or SBF flats are allocated to eligible applicants.
sections.Who is this for?: You and your family have been living in a HDB public rental flat for at least 2 years.
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your HFE letter application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

title: Third Child Priority Scheme (TCPS)
description: Provides priority in flat allocation to eligible families with 3 or more children.
highlights: Up to 10% of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats, and up to 10% of Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) flats allocated for eligible families with 3 or more children
Provides an additional ballot chance to secure a flat

sections.About this support:
- Up to 10% of BTO flats, and up to 10% of SBF flats allocated for eligible families
- Parent(s) expecting their third child can apply for a flat under the TCPS subject to meeting all other eligibility conditions
sections.Who is this for?:
- You and/or your spouse are Singapore Citizens
- If you are divorced or widowed, you must be a Singapore Citizen to qualify
- Your family must consist of at least 3 children or be expecting a third child who are from a legal marriage or legally adopted
- If the family is expecting*, you must have a doctor’s certificate confirming the pregnancy
- Divorced parents must have legal custody, care, and control of their children
- Adoptive parents must provide the Adoption Order when applying for a flat
- Your third child must be born on or after 1 January 1987
- Your youngest child or the child you are expecting must be a Singapore Citizen
- Your other children must be either Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents
- You have not previously bought a flat under the TCPS

*This includes cases where the parent(s) have 1 child and are expecting 2 or more children, or where the parent(s) do not have a child yet and are expecting 3 or more children.
sections.How to apply?:
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your HFE letter application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

title: CareShield Life / ElderShield Supplements
description: Provides additional benefits, like higher payouts, for CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholders.
highlights: Supplement premiums can be paid using cash or MediSave for flexibility in payment
Can acquire multiple supplement policies to suit your needs
Grants extra coverage in addition to your existing CareShield Life or ElderShield plan

sections.About this support:
- Complements your CareShield Life or ElderShield plan with enhanced coverage, providing extra benefits such as increased monthly payouts
- Flexibility to buy multiple supplement policies for enhanced coverage
- Premiums for Supplements can be paid thru cash or by using your or your family member’s MediSave, limited to $600 per calendar year per insured person
- If you have existing Supplements under ElderShield and choose to join CareShield Life, you may continue to maintain your previous policy and can claim from both
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Existing CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholder
sections.How to apply?:
- Application for plans is done through the individual insurers
- To review and compare Supplement plans, you may:
  - visit insurer websites or contact them directly for plan details.
  - read more about Supplements and see the [comparison charts available online for CareShield Life and ElderShield supplements](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/careshield-life/careshield-life-and-eldershield-supplements)
sections.Phone number:
Healthcare Hotline: [1800-222-3399](tel:1800-222-3399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: CareShield Life Premium Subsidies
description: To ensure that CareShield Life premiums are affordable, the Government has committed to providing several premium support measures, such as Premium Subsidies, Participation Incentives and Additional Participation Incentives for Merdeka and Pioneer Generation.
highlights: Means-tested CareShield Life Premium Subsidies of up to 30%

sections.About this support:
- Means-tested Premium Subsidies of up to 30% for eligible lower- to middle-income households
- Transitional support will also be provided to all policyholders to help manage the premium increases from 2026 to 2029, following the CareShield Life 2025 Review
- Participation Incentives for Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier who joined and were covered under CareShield Life between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024: Up to $1,875 ($187.50/year)
- Additional Participation Incentives for Pioneer and Merdeka Generation citizens who joined and were covered under CareShield Life between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024: $1,125 ($112.50/year)
- Participation incentives and Additional Participation Incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and used to offset premiums payable for each year
sections.Who is this for?:
**Eligibility for means-tested Premium Subsidies:**

- Subsidies of up to 30% for eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Permanent Residents will receive half the subsidy rate applicable for Singapore Citizens
- Household monthly income per person of $3,600 or below
- Living in residences with an Annual Value (AV) of $31,000 and below
- Not owning more than 1 property

As of 1 Jan 2025,

Note: The above subsidy rates apply to those living in residences with an AV of $21,000 or less. Residences with an AV between $21,001 and $31,000 receive 10% less subsidies. Those who live in residences with an AV above $31,000 or own multiple properties will not receive these subsidies.

**Eligibility for Participation Incentives:**

- For Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier who joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024
- Depending on birth year
- Total Participation Incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and used to offset premiums payable for each year

**Eligibility for Additional Participation Incentives:**

- For Merdeka and Pioneer Generation seniors who joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024
- Provided on top of Participation Incentives
- Total Participation Incentives provided will be spread equally over 10 years and used to offset premiums payable for each year

All policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums. Transitional support is directly provided to policyholders. Policyholders do not need to apply for this support.

sections.How to apply?: The subsidies that you are eligible for will be automatically applied to your CareShield Life premiums.
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only
sections.Agency website: Please click [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/careshield-life/careshield-premiums-and-subsidies) for more information on Premium Subsidies, Participation Incentives and Additional Participation Incentives.
sections.Phone number:
Healthcare Hotline: [1800-222-3399](tel:1800-222-3399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: ITE Monthly Financial Assistance Scheme (MFAS)
description: Provides a monthly allowance to full-time Singaporean students from lower-income households who need regular financial assistance for daily expenses.
highlights: Monthly allowance of $200 per month with effect from Academic Year 2026
Apply online via the ITE portal. Click on iStudent icon > Financial Assistance icon.

sections.About this support:
- Monthly allowance of $200 per month
- The number of months of award will depend on the needs of each individual student
sections.Who is this for?: Full-time Singaporean ITE students who require regular financial assistance
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply online via the [ITE portal](https://myite.ite.edu.sg/)

If you need more help, refer to the [step by step guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/c7a7f637-986d-483a-9766-a19bccd726c0/Step By Step Guide on Applying Financial Assistance_Bursary_15 Sep 25.pdf).

title: Infant and Childcare Subsidies
description: Provides tiered subsidies to help cover infant care and childcare fees for Singapore Citizen children from different income backgrounds.
highlights: Working applicants: Basic Subsidy of $600 for infant care and $300 for childcare
Non-working applicants: Basic Subsidy of $150 for infant care and childcare
Additional Subsidy for working applicants

sections.About this support:
**Working applicants (mother or single father who works at least 56 hours per month)**

- Basic Subsidy of $600 for infant care and $300 for childcare
- Additional Subsidy of up to $710 for infant care and up to $467 for childcare

**Non-working applicants**

- Basic Subsidy of $150 for infant care and childcare
- Eligible applicants who are not working or who are non-parent caregivers can apply for Special Approval to receive the higher Basic Subsidy and Additional Subsidy that working applicants receive
sections.Who is this for?:
Types of subsidies
Eligibility criteria
For all subsidies
- Child must be a Singapore Citizen
- Enrolled in an infant care or childcare centre licensed by ECDA
Additional Subsidy
- Working applicants (mother or single father who works at least 56 hours per month)
- Monthly household income of up to $12,000, or monthly household income per capita of up to $3,000 for larger families with 5 or more family members in the same household
  - From 1 January 2027, monthly household income thresholds will be raised to $15,000, or $3,400 per capita
Special Approval
- Main subsidy applicants who are not working due to the following reasons:
  - Looking for a job
  - Studying, training, or on course for at least 56 hours a month
  - Pregnancy
  - Medically unfit for work due to hospitalisation, long-term illness and/or permanent disability
  - Taking care of a special needs child
  - Taking care of a sick family member who requires a full-time caregiver
  - Caring full-time for a younger child aged 24 months and below who is not enrolled in a preschool
  - Incarcerated
  - Non-parent caregivers who are caring for the child such as grandparents, legal guardian, foster parents, and head of a children’s home
- Families who are tenants of a rental flat under the HDB’s Public Rental Scheme or are beneficiaries of ComCare Short-To-Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) or Long-Term-Assistance (LTA) will automatically qualify for maximum preschool subsidies upon application for Special Approval
sections.How to apply?: Refer to Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) [website](https://www.ecda.gov.sg/parents/preschool-subsidies/how-to-apply-or-make-changes-to-subsidies) to apply or make changes to subsidies

title: Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS) and KiFAS Startup Grant (SUG)
description: Provides subsidies for kindergarten programmes to ensure affordability for low and middle-income Singapore Citizen families, along with an annual KiFAS Start-Up Grant (SUG) to assist low-income families with initial costs.
highlights: Subsidies range between $17 and $161 per month
Eligible families will receive an additional yearly SUG (capped at $240 per year) to cover initial costs
Apply at your child's kindergarten

sections.About this support:
- Subsidies range between $17 and $161 per month
- Subsidy amount depends on monthly household income, and will be directly disbursed to the child's kindergarten
- Eligible applicants will receive a yearly KiFAS SUG capped at $240 per year to help cover initial costs such as registration fee, deposit, school uniform, insurance, and educational material fees, in addition to the basic subsidies
sections.Who is this for?:
- Child must be a Singapore Citizen
- Enrolled in an Anchor Operator or Ministry of Education Kindergarten
- Monthly household income of up to $12,000, or monthly household income per capita of up to $3,000 for larger families with 5 or more family members in the same household
  - From 1 January 2027, monthly household income thresholds will be raised to $15,000, or $3,400 per capita
- Yearly SUG:

title: Change in HDB Flat Ownership After Flat Owner's Demise
description: Retain your HDB flat following the demise of joint owner or sole owner/tenant-in-common.
highlights: Family structures changes may affect flat retention eligibility

sections.About this support:
Take over interest in the HDB flat held under joint-tenancy, when you lodge a Notice of Death with the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), or

Register your right to administer the estate of the deceased sole owner/ co-owner of HDB flat held under tenancy-in-common as the Administrator or Executor, and effect an ownership change in the HDB flat to the beneficiaries.
sections.Who is this for?:
As the remaining family or single occupier, you can retain the existing flat provided you:

- Are a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is at least 21 years old; and
- Satisfy the eligibility rules and conditions to own a flat.
sections.How to apply?:
**For demise of joint owner**
Lodging a Notice of Death
For flats held under joint-tenancy, the remaining joint-owners can lodge the Notice of Death personally at [SLA's FAQ](https://www.sla.gov.sg/frequently-asked-questions-faqs) ( How do I lodge a Notice of Death to inform SLA of the death of a joint owner), appoint your own solicitor to lodge the Notice of Death on your behalf or engage HDB’s services to lodge the Notice of Death.
If you wish to engage HDB’s services to handle the Notice of Death,  you must bring along these documents to lodge a Notice of Death:
- Identity cards of remaining joint-owners
- Original death certificate or e-death certificate of deceased owner
- Title document (if any)
- Pay the registration and conveyancing fees at the point of application.
HDB’s Legal Group will then prepare the Notice of Death and inform the remaining joint-owners to sign the documents at the HDB Branch managing the flat.
**For demise of sole owner/tenant-in-common**
Grant of Probate
- If there is a will, the deceased's interest in the flat will be distributed according to the will. You will need the Grant of Probate.
- The deceased’s family should engage a private solicitor to apply for this court order, which gives legal authority to the Executor (the person named in the will) to manage the deceased's estate.
Grant of Letters of Administration
- If there is no will, the deceased’s interest in the flat will be distributed according to the provisions of the Intestate Succession Act. You will need the Grant of Letters of Administration.
- The deceased’s family should engage a private solicitor to apply for this court order, which gives legal authority to the Administrator to manage the deceased’s estate.

Once the Grant of Letters of Administration or the Grant of Probate has been obtained, you can engage your own solicitors or appoint HDB's solicitors to act for you to register your legal right as the Administrator or Executor. You may also approach the HDB Branch managing the deceased’s flat to make the necessary application with the following documents:

- Original copy of the Grant of Letters of Administration and Statement for Grant of Letters of Administration or Grant of Probate and will
- Original copy of the Syariah Court Inheritance Certificate (for Muslim estates only)
- A copy of the deceased owner’s death certificate or e-death certificate
- Title document of the deceased’s flat
- Identity card(s) of all flat owner(s) and Administrator(s) or Executor(s)

If you are an Administrator/ Executor and engage HDB's services to act for you in the transaction, you will have to:

- Sign  the relevant documents
- Pay fees (stamp fees, conveyancing fees, etc.)
- Apply to HDB to effect an ownership change of the flat upon completion of the transaction either via a change of flat ownership to eligible beneficiaries or a resale of part-share, subject to the beneficiaries meeting the eligibility conditions.

ComLink+ families will receive financial top-ups through ComLink+ Progress Packages when they take active steps towards their longer-term goals in the areas of preschool education, employment, debt clearance, and home ownership

sections.About this support:

- [Revised – from Q3 2026] Up to $250 per quarter for regular preschool attendance

title: MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN)
description: All Singapore Citizen newborns are eligible for the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) of up to $5,000.
highlights: MediSave Grant of $5,000 for Singapore Citizen Newborns
4% annual interest
Grant can cover MediShield Life premiums, vaccinations, hospitalisation and outpatient treatments

sections.About this support:
- Up to $5,000 credited to each Singapore Citizen newborn's CPF MediSave account
- Accounts are opened automatically for newborns
- Covers MediShield Life premiums, recommended childhood vaccinations, hospitalisation, and approved outpatient treatments
sections.Who is this for?:
- All Singapore Citizen newborns born on or after 26 August 2012 are eligible for MGN
- Children who are Singapore Citizens at birth and born before January 1, 2015, are entitled to MGN of up to $3,000
  - For those born on or after January 1, 2015, they are eligible for MGN of $4,000
  - For those born on or after April 1, 2025, they are eligible for MGN of $5,000
- Children who are born overseas can qualify for MGN upon registering their birth with Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or through a Singapore Overseas Mission
  - The MGN amount will depend on the date that the child becomes a Singapore Citizen
  - Children who obtain Singapore Citizenship after the age of 2 are not eligible for MGN.
sections.How to apply?:

- The grant is automatically credited into your newborn’s MediSave account within 1 week from birth registration / acquiring Singapore citizenship
- Once the MGN has been credited, you will receive a notification on the MGN amount

Available at both private and public Assisted Reproduction centres

description: Provides community-based mental health assessment, therapeutic intervention, case management for youths with mild mental health conditions while monitoring and checking in with the youth before, during and after intervention has been provided.

sections.About this support:

- Provide mental health assessments and support youths in understanding and identifying their care needs.
- Provide coordinated person-centric care intervention and support for youths and their caregivers through providing assessments, therapeutic intervention and case management.
- Engage community and healthcare partners to build a supportive environment for youths with mental health conditions through active collaboration and co-management of cases.
- Facilitate the formation of supportive relationships with families and peers in the recovery journey of youths.

These community mental health teams are developed under the Community Mental Health Masterplan driven by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), together with the Ministry of Health (MOH). The teams are fully funded by the government and there is no out-of-pocket cost.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Youths at higher risk for mental health conditions, their families and their support systems.
- Aged 12 to 25 years old
sections.How to apply?:

title: Fostering Scheme
description: Provides a safe and nurturing family environment for children needing care and protection, offering love, stability, and essentials like food and shelter. Foster families create positive family experiences, demonstrating care and concern, with the aim to reunite children with their birth families once safe to do so.
highlights: Allows children in need to benefit from a nurturing home environment that facilitates their growth and enables them to fulfil their potential

Support services are available for foster families, including fostering allowance to defray the cost of caring for the child, training for foster parents, and support and guidance from Foster Care Worker and other professionals
Aims to continue building up a diverse pool of foster parents to meet the different needs of foster children

sections.About this support:
- Monthly fostering allowance of $1,100 for each foster child, or $1,500 for a child with special needs
- Childcare subsidies with a monthly co-payment of $200 for full-day care and $150 for half-day care to be paid by foster parents
- Student care subsidies with a monthly co-payment of $80 to be paid by foster parents for MSF-registered centres
- Medical subsidies cover medical treatment at public healthcare institutions (polyclinics, public hospitals, and public specialist centres)
  - Foster children also receive subsidies at participating CHAS General Practitioners and dental clinics
- Support and guidance from Foster Care Worker attached to every foster parent
- Training courses conducted by Social Service Institute for new foster parents
- Immediate support via an emergency hotline available 24/7
- Support groups and respite care available
- Foster parents enjoy childcare leave benefits, just as birth parents do under the Child Development Co-Savings Act and Employment Act
sections.Who is this for?:
- At least 25 years old
- Married and applying as a couple
- Medically fit to care for children
- Minimum secondary school education
- Minimum monthly household income of $2,000 and per capita income of at least $700 (Retirees can apply to be assessed based on non-work sources of income and saving)
- Provide a child-safe home environment, which includes commitment not to use physical punishment, and installation of window grilles for foster children below 13 years old
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply online through the [MSF Fostering Scheme portal](https://volunteer.gov.sg/scheme-detail?code=fostering):
  - Click "Apply"
  - Register or sign in
  - Fill in the application form
  - Upload supporting documents
- MSF or an appointed agency will contact you within three working days
- The assessment include:
  - Interview session(s)
  - Home Visit
  - Medical screenings
- After approval:
  - Attend mandatory training sessions
  - Await foster child placement
sections.Phone number:
MSF Consolidated Hotline: [1800-111-2222](tel:1800-111-2222) 
To reach the Fostering division, say "Foster" when prompted by the virtual assistant.

title: Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB)
description: Provides up to 4 weeks of income support, for eligible working fathers who do not qualify for Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL).
highlights: For children born or adopted before 1 Jan 2024, eligible fathers can receive up to 2 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) , capped at $2,500 per week.
For children born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2024, eligible fathers can receive up to 4 weeks of GPPB, capped at $2,500 per week.
For natural or adoptive fathers who do not qualify for GPPL due to their employment arrangement

sections.About this support:
- Up to 2 weeks of income support for eligible fathers for child born/estimated delivery/FIA date before January 1, 2024, capped at $2,500 per week.
- Up to 4 weeks of income support for eligible fathers for child born/estimated delivery date/FIA on or after January 1, 2024, capped at $2,500 per week.
sections.Who is this for?:
**For natural fathers with live births**:

- Your child’s date of birth/estimated delivery date is on or after 1 Jan 2021.
  - Your child is a Singapore Citizen or becomes one within 12 months of birth

**For natural fathers with stillbirths**:

- The date of stillbirth is on or after November 1, 2021
- Either you or the child’s mother is a Singapore citizen

**For adoptive fathers**:

- You are not the natural father of the child
- Your FIA date is on or after 1 Jan 2021
- The child must be below 12 months old on FIA date
- If child is not a Singapore citizen, a dependent’s pass (DP) has been issued and either you or your wife are Singapore citizens.

**Applicable to all**:

- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before child's birth
- Lawfully married to the child's mother between conception and birth or within 12 months of birth
- Not eligible for Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) except under specific conditions such as end of employment contract or retrenchment
sections.How to apply?:
- Record employment or self-employment details for the 12 months before your child's birth or Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date.
- Submit your claim online [here](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 15 months of your child's birth or FIA date.
- An officer will contact you following your submission.
sections.Phone number:
MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222) 
(say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

title: Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL)
description: Provides up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL), for eligible working fathers.
highlights: Up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for eligible fathers
Government reimbursement/payment for GPPL capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000

sections.About this support:
**Child born/FIA/estimated delivery date before 1 Jan 2024**:

- Up to 2 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for fathers, to be taken within 12 months from the child's date of birth.
- Government reimbursement for all 2 weeks of GPPL, capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $5,000.

**Child born/FIA/estimated delivery date between 1 Jan 2024 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)**:

- Up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for fathers, to be taken within 12 months from the child's date of birth.
- Government reimbursement for all 4 weeks of GPPL, capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000.
- Weeks 3-4 are additional, and employers can grant on a voluntary basis

**Child born/FIA/estimated delivery date on or after 1 Apr 2025:**

- Up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for fathers, to be taken within 12 months from the child’s date of birth.
- Government reimbursement for all 4 weeks of GPPL, capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000.
sections.Who is this for?:
**For natural fathers with live births**:

- Child born or estimated delivery date on or after January 1, 2017
- Child is a Singapore Citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth
- Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth
- Served employer for at least 3 months before child's birth
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before child's birth

**For natural fathers with stillborn children**:

- Stillbirth occurred on or after November 1, 2021
- Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and stillbirth or within 12 months from stillbirth, and either you or the child’s mother are Singapore citizens
- Served employer for at least 3 months before the date of stillbirth
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before the date of stillbirth

**For adoptive fathers**:

- Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date on or after January 1, 2017
- Not the natural father of the child
- If child is not a Singapore Citizen, either you or your wife must be a Singapore Citizen since the child's Dependant's Pass issuance
- Served employer for at least 3 months before FIA date
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before FIA date
sections.How to apply?:
**For employees**:

- Notify your employer about your leave arrangement early.
- Submit the [declaration form (GPPL1)](https://file.go.gov.sg/gppl1form.pdf) to your employer with all necessary supporting documents.
- Apply for leave according to your employer's procedures.

**For self-employed**:

- Record your leave dates.
- Submit your claim online via the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL)](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/login?redirect=eservices/submit-a-claim) Portal within 3 months after your leave.
- Check your application status on the GPL Portal.

**For employers**:

- Obtain and verify the [declaration form (GPPL1)](https://file.go.gov.sg/gppl1form.pdf) from your employee.
- Keep the declaration form or records for 5 years from the last leave date.
- Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the GPL Portal within 3 months after your employee's leave.
- Check your application status on the GPL Portal.

title: Tax Reliefs
description: Provides tax reliefs to taxpayers who support family members in need, inclusive of dependants with disabilities.
highlights: Provides up to $14,000 of tax relief for taxpayers who support family members in need, inclusive of dependants with disabilities or impairment

sections.About this support:
- [**Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR) **](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/cVyhpH3s/grandparent-caregiver-relief-gcr)

Provides tax relief of up to $3,000 to working mothers who engage their parents, grandparents or in-laws as caregivers for their children.

- [**Parent Relief/ Parent Relief (Disability)**](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/TAX_RELIEF_CAREGIVERS_DISABLED/parent-reliefparent-relief-disability)

Provides tax relief of up to $14,000 per dependant for individuals supporting their parents, grandparents or in-laws, with additional relief for dependants with disabilities.

- [**Sibling Relief (Disability)**](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/U3ip0GiR/sibling-relief-disability)

sections.Who is this for?:
- Working mothers (married, divorced, or widowed) with a Singaporean child under 12/unmarried child with disabilities and caregiver/s that resides in Singapore

- Taxpayers supporting dependant/s aged 55 and above, including those with disabilities, living in their household.

title: Strengthening Families Programme (FAM)
description: Provides divorce support and family counselling to all families.

sections.About this support:
- Provides specialised services and programmes for families facing early signs of stress, as well as divorcing and divorced families.
- These support services include marriage and divorce support programmes, and a family counselling service.
- For Minor couples who are marrying, they are required to attend a complimentary mandatory Marriage Preparation Programme (MPrep - required by law) provided by the agency.
- Young couples are also encouraged to attend the MPrep before they marry.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Divorcing and divorced families
- Families facing marital, parenting or intrapersonal issues
- Individuals/couples below 21 years old need to seek parental or guardian (who is above 21 years old) consent.
- Strengthening Families Programme (Fei Yue - Choa Chu Kang) and Strengthening Families Programme (Care Corner - Tampines) also provide marriage support for civil minor couples (either one or both parties under 18 years old), civil young couples (groom aged between 21 and 24, bride 21 & above), and transnational couples
sections.How to apply?: Apply through phone calls, emails, walk-in, or referrals by other agencies.
sections.What to expect?:
- Individuals/couples can contact the agency to request for more information on services.
- Agency worker will conduct an enquiry and intake assessment for suitability and appropriate services required.

title: MediFund
description: For Singaporeans who face difficulties with remaining medical bills after receiving government subsidies and other means of payment.
highlights: Assistance with medical bills
Amount of assistance depends on the applicant's circumstances and bills incurred
Apply through Medical Social Workers at the institution where you received treatment

sections.About this support: The actual amount of assistance you receive depends on you and your family members' financial, health and social circumstances, as well as the size of the medical bill incurred.
sections.How to apply?:
- You or your family can approach the Medical Social Workers at the MediFund-approved institution at which you had treatment
- In addition to MediFund, they will also be able to explore other possible financing means with you
sections.Phone number:
MediFund applications are administered directly by the MediFund-approved institution. You may wish to first contact the Medical Social Services Department or Business Office Department of the institution you are seeking care at for further assistance.

MOH Hotline: [6325 9220](tel:63259220)

title: Transitional Shelter (TS)
description: Provide temporary accommodation and social work intervention to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.

sections.About this support:
- Transitional Shelter (TS) provides temporary accommodation to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.
- It provides onsite social work intervention to address the complex needs of the admitted families/individuals to achieve long-term and stable housing.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident
- Exhausted all other means of accommodation and facing financial difficulties
- Require social work intervention and willing to work with caseworkers to achieve long-term housing
- Able to live independently in the community, in a communal shelter setting (i.e. does not require close supervision or nursing care)
sections.How to apply?:
- You may contact your nearest Family Service Centre (FSC) for assistance if you are homeless.
- The TS will only accept applications from FSCs and other community agencies with social work competencies that can assess whether the family/individual meets the admission criteria.
- The referring agency will need to send in the application form, social report and supporting documents to TS for assessment.

To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, call Comcare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving referral, the TS will conduct an intake assessment to ensure that the applicant is eligible for the shelter.
- Clients must work with the TS on case goals and intervention plans to achieve long-term stable housing eventually.

title: ITE Special Student Assistance Scheme (SSAS)

highlights: One-off financial assistance from $100 to $400
Apply online via the ITE portal. Click on iStudent icon > Financial Assistance icon.

sections.About this support:
- One-off financial assistance from $100 to $400
- The amount will depend on the needs of each individual student

sections.How to apply?:
You can apply online via the [ITE portal](https://myite.ite.edu.sg/)

If you need more help, refer to the [step by step guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/c7a7f637-986d-483a-9766-a19bccd726c0/Step By Step Guide on Applying Financial Assistance_Bursary_15 Sep 25.pdf).

title: Marriage Preparation Programme for Minor and Young Muslim Couples
description: Provides pre- and post-marriage support for minor and young couples.

sections.About this support: Supports minor and young couples through premarital consultation session, marriage preparation workshops, and parents support group.
sections.Who is this for?:
Minor Couples (Mandatory to complete Marriage Preparation Programme before applying for marriage):

- Either party is below 21 years old
- At least one party is Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Both bride and groom are Muslims

Young Couples:

- Groom is between 21 and 24 years old and bride is aged 21 years and above
- At least one party is Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Both bride and groom are Muslims
sections.How to apply?: Call, email, visit or through referrals by other agencies to apply.
sections.What to expect?:
**For minor couples**

- Sign up (email or call) directly with the agency for the mandatory (requried by law) complimentary Marriage Preparation Programme (MPP) before proceeding with marriage application via Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) website.
- Upon completion of MPP, the agency will provide casework and counselling if necessary for up to 10 years and refer couples with higher risks to FSC or SSO.
- Eligible couples will also be auto-referred to KidStart. Those who prefer not to be auto-referred, can complete an opt out form instead for the agency to follow-up with them.

**For young couples**

- Similar as above, except that the MPP is not mandatory for young couples.
- They can apply e-file for marriage (OMJ) before attending MPP.
- Upon completion of the MPP, the other services offered to minor couples are applicable to young couples too.

title: Disabled Persons Scheme (DPS)
description: Eligible drivers are exempted from paying the premium for the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) when they purchase a vehicle.
highlights: Exemption from Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and Additional Registration Fee (ARF) for eligible persons with disabilities who are gainfully employed and need a vehicle to earn a living
For Singaporean Citizens with permanent physical disabilities who are medically certified as permanently disabled and incapable of taking public transport (i.e. bus and/or MRT), but fit to drive

sections.About this support: - Eligible drivers are exempted from paying the ​premium for the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) when they purchase a vehicle
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen
- Persons with permanent physical disabilities who are medically certified by doctors from the Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Clinic for Advanced Rehabilitation Therapeutics (CART) as permanently disabled and incapable of taking public transport (i.e. bus and/or MRT), but fit to drive
- Gainfully employed and need a vehicle to earn a living
- Possesses a valid Class 3 Driving Licence
- In the 30th income percentile or below where household income does not exceed $6,500 for a 4-member household
- Vehicle must meet all of the following specifications:
  - Engine capacity must not be more than 1,600cc
  - Maximum power output of not more than 97kW (130bhp)
  - Open Market Value (OMV) of not more than S$20,000
sections.How to apply?: For more information on the application process, please visit [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/disabled-persons-scheme).

title: Child Protection Specialist Centre (CPSC)
description: Serves as specialists on child protection matters to provide community-based support to children who face abuse or neglect at home.

sections.About this support:
Child Protection Specialist Centres (CPSCs) provide child-centric, family-focused and community-based support to children who face abuse or neglect at home.

Support provided includes:

- Safety planning
- Casework intervention
- Counselling to address the risks posed to the children and young persons
- Practical and other relevant services to the children and young persons and their families
sections.Who is this for?: Children and young persons who face abuse or neglect at home.
sections.How to apply?:
- Referral is required.
- Contact CPSC via phone call or email to enquire on the referral process.
sections.What to expect?:
- After receiving the referral, the social worker from CPSC will contact the referring person to find out more about the presenting abuse or neglect concerns.
- The CPSC will then inform on whether the referral is assessed to be suitable for CPSC to provide the intervention.
- If assessed to not be suitable, CPSC will advise on the other possible services or contact points.

title: Life Insurance Relief
description: Provides tax relief of up to $5,000 for individuals who paid annual insurance premiums on their own life insurance policies.
highlights: Life Insurance Relief up to $5,000

sections.About this support:
- Tax relief for your life insurance premiums
- If you are a married man, you may also claim the life insurance premium paid for your wife
- The amount of relief is capped between the lower of:
  - Difference between $5,000 and your CPF contribution; or
  - Up to 7% of the insured value of your own / your wife's life, or the amount of insurance premiums paid
sections.Who is this for?:
To claim Life Insurance Relief, you must meet all the following conditions:

- You have paid, and are claiming, for your own life insurance policy
- Married men may also claim for premiums paid on their wife’s life insurance policy
- The insurance company has an office or branch in Singapore
  - The Singapore office of the insurance company should perform similar activities as the overseas company where the life insurance policy was purchased
- Your / your wife’s total CPF contributions for the following were less than $5,000 in the previous year:
  - Compulsory employee's CPF contribution
  - Compulsory MediSave or voluntary CPF contribution for self-employed individuals

For paper filing:

highlights: Spouse Relief of $2,000, up to $5,500 for spouse with disability or mental impairment

sections.About this support:
- Spouse Relief of $2,000 for taxpayers who have supported their spouses
- Spouse Relief (Disability) of $5,500 for taxpayers who have supported their spouses with disabilities
sections.Who is this for?:
**For Spouse Relief:**

You must fulfil all these conditions in the previous year:

- Your spouse has been living with / supported by you
- Your spouse did not have an annual income of more than $8,000
- You have made maintenance payments under a Court Order or Deed of Separation (if you are legally separated from your spouse)

title: Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR)
description: Provides tax relief of up to $3,000 to working mothers who engage their parents, grandparents, parents-in-law or grandparents-in-law as caregivers for their children.
highlights: Claim $3,000 for Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR)

sections.About this support:
- Eligible working mother can claim relief of $3,000
- Caregiver may be the subject of other relief claims e.g. Parent Relief, Spouse Relief
sections.Who is this for?:
To be eligible for GCR, you must meet all the following conditions:

- Working mother who is married, divorced or widowed
- Caregiver resides and lives in Singapore^
- Caregiver is a parent / grandparent / parent-in-law / grandparent-in-law (in-laws include that of ex-spouses')
- As of last year, caregiver has been looking after a Singapore Citizen child aged 12 and below / an unmarried child with disabilities
- Caregiver's annual income did not exceed $8,000 from any trade, business, profession, vocation and / or employment in the previous year
- No one else has claimed GCR on the same caregiver. Relief is limited to 1 claim for 1 parent / grandparent i.e. a single claim of $3,000

^ Dependant has been staying in Singapore on a permanent basis. Foreign dependants must have stayed in Singapore for at least 8 months in the previous year.
sections.How to apply?:
**For e-Filing:**

- If claiming the relief for the first time:

**For paper filing:**

- For Form B1 & B, fill in the “Grandparent Caregiver Relief” section.
- Include your dependant's details in Appendix 2 as well, if it’s your first time claiming GCR

title: MediShield Life

highlights: Lifetime coverage for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents regardless of age or health condition

sections.About this support:
- Provides [lifetime coverage](https://moh.gov.sg/home/our-healthcare-system/medishield-life/what-is-medishield-life/what-medishield-life-benefits) for hospital bills and selected outpatient treatments
- MediShield Life coverage is sized for subsidised treatment in public hospitals and pegged at B2/C-type wards
- If you choose to stay in an A/B1-type ward or in a private hospital, you are still covered by MediShield Life
  - However, your MediShield Life payout will cover only a proportion of your bill, and you would need to draw from MediSave and/or cash to pay the balance
sections.Who is this for?: - Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
sections.How to apply?: No application is required
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Healthcare Hotline: [1800 222 3399](tel:1800-222-3399)

title: MediSave
description: A personal healthcare savings account that helps you pay for you and loved ones' healthcare expenses over your lifetime, especially when you retire and no longer have regular income.
highlights: Covers selected medical, treatment and hospital expenses, up to the approved limits
Covers for healthcare insurance premiums, rehabilitation and palliative care
Applicable at all MediSave accredited Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs)

sections.About this support:
- MediSave pays for a variety of medical expenses such as selected outpatient treatments, day surgery and hospitalisation expenses
- It also covers the costs for your rehabilitation and palliative care
- You can also tap on your MediSave to pay for health insurance premiums for yourself and your loved ones
sections.Who is this for?:
- You need to be a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR)
- Your spouse, children and parents can be of any nationality, except grandparents and siblings who must be SC or PR
sections.How to apply?:
- To use your MediSave, inform the Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs) or Medical Institutions (MIs) where you are receiving treatment at, and you would like to use your MediSave to pay for your medical expenses
  - If this is your first time applying, you will need to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)
  - If you had previously given a standing authorisation for the use of MediSave, the MI will submit a claim on your behalf
- The PHI and/or MI will submit the medical claim on your behalf and payment from your healthcare plans will be made directly to them
- Upon approval of the claim, the Board and/or insurer will notify you accordingly
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)
Note: By appointment only
sections.Phone number:
Healthcare Hotline: [1800 222 3399](tel:18002223399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: ActiveSG Membership
description: A national movement for individuals, families and communities to experience and share the joy of living better through sports.
highlights: Free entry to ActiveSG swimming pools and gyms for Singaporeans aged 65 and above

sections.About this support:
- Swimming complexes and gym admissions
- Payment for ActiveSG programmes and activities (up to 30% of the programme price)
- Booking of ActiveSG sport facilities
- Purchase of MyActiveGYM™ and MyActiveSWIM™ schemes

Other benefits:

- Eligibility to purchase MyActiveGYM™ and MyActiveSWIM™ schemes
- Supplementary membership – parents/legal guardians can apply for supplementary membership for children under 15 years old
- Active Health Lab access

title: Tax Payment Support
description: Supports eligible individuals in their tax payments through various payment arrangements such as longer GIRO-based instalment plans.
highlights: Enables longer payment plans for applicants experiencing difficulties in paying their taxes
Grants retirees the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), offering longer instalment plans for tax payment

sections.About this support:
- Longer instalment plans may be made available for individuals or businesses facing financial challenges or other extenuating circumstances
- Eligible retirees may apply for the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), which provides a longer instalment plan of up to 24 months for property tax payment
sections.Who is this for?:
For individuals who experience unexpected or extenuating circumstances due to the following:

- Financial issues
- High medical expenses
- Loss of employment or income
- Lawsuits
  - You may be required to submit documentary evidence to support your request for a longer instalment plan

For retirees:

- To be eligible for the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), applicants must meet all the following conditions:
  - You are residing in the property (and taxed at owner-occupier tax rates)
  - Your assessable income for Year of Assessment 2023 does not exceed $34,000
  - All property owners, including yourself, are aged 65 or above in 2024
  - There is outstanding property tax payable for the property

If applicants cease to be eligible, their extended instalment plan will be reverted to the standard instalment plan
sections.How to apply?:
For individuals:
- Apply for an extended instalment plan via the 'Apply for Payment Plan' digital service through the IRAS [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg)
  - Please note that instalment plans are only available with GIRO
- For existing GIRO users, cancel your current plan and set up a new one. You may refer to this guide on [cancelling and reactivating GIRO for detailed instructions](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/pdf/steps-to-cancel-and-reactivate-giro---enf-webpages@18feb2020.pdf?sfvrsn=fbc17716_5)
- For applicants without a GIRO arrangement for Individual Income and Property Tax, you may apply for GIRO (with a DBS / POSB or OCBC bank account) via [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg) and set up your new plan online. Refer to [this guide](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/payments/experiencing-difficulties-in-paying-your-tax) for detailed instructions
For businesses without an existing GIRO arrangement for Corporate Income Tax, Property Tax and Goods and Services Tax:
- Apply for GIRO with a DBS / POSB, OCBC, UOB, Bank of China or Maybank account via the IRAS [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg)
- Arrange a new plan
- Alternatively, [you may refer to this guide for the detailed steps](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/pdf/eservice-user-guide_apply-for-payment-plan_non-individuals_2023-11.pdf?sfvrsn=31c2fac6_3)

Where you do not have account with any of the participating banks listed above, you may:

- Fill up [this form ](https://form.gov.sg/673c038018eb14d441d54153)to request for GIRO application form
- View on applying GIRO [here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax)

Please refer to [IRAS’ site on alternative tax payment plans for more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/payments/experiencing-difficulties-in-paying-your-tax)

title: Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR)
description: Provides a one-off tax rebate of up to $20,000 per child to eligible parents to encourage them to have more children.
highlights: Tax rebate of up to $20,000 per child for eligible parents
Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR) may be shared between parents based on an agreed apportionment
Unutilised balance can be carried forward to offset future tax payable and / or transferred between spouses

sections.About this support:
- Rebate amount increases for each child, with $5,000 for the first, $10,000 for the second and $20,000 for all subsequent children
- Parents may share the PTR based on an agreed apportionment
- Unutilised PTR will be carried forward to offset future income tax payable
  - It may also be transferred online via myTaxPortal between spouses
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore tax residents who are married, divorced or widowed in the relevant year
- Different qualifying conditions for your child will apply based on the following:
  - Children born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2008
  - Children born or adopted before 1 Jan 2008
    - Please note that PTR is not available for your first child as well as from your fifth child onwards
  - Child is a Singapore Citizen at the time of birth/marriage/legal adoption or within 12 months thereafter
- Additional conditions determining your eligibility are as follows:
  - Children given for adoption
  - If married is dissolved under a court order
  - If spouse passes away
- For more information on the qualifying conditions, please visit [IRAS’ PTR page](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/parenthood-tax-rebate-(ptr))
- Applicants may use the [PTR Eligibility Tool](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/individual-income-tax/employees/ptr-calculator.xlsm?sfvrsn=e185c04f_17) to check their eligibility
sections.How to apply?:
**For e-Filing:**

If this is your first time claiming this relief:

- Log in with Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
- Navigate to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
- Select “File” to File Income Tax Return
- Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
- Select “Add New” > “Child/Parenthood Tax Rebate”
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Yes” under “Claim one-time Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR) to indicate share of PTR as agreed by you and your Spouse"
- Select “Update"

If you have claimed this relief before, any unutilised balance will be carried forward automatically to offset future tax payable

**For paper filing:**

- Complete the particulars of your child in Appendix 2 of Form B1 & B if this is your first time claiming this relief
- If you have claimed this relief before, any unutilised balance will be carried forward without further action

title: NSman Relief
description: Provides tax relief to eligible operationally ready National Servicemen (NSmen) to recognise their contributions to National Service, as well as to the wives and parents of NSmen to recognise the support they give to their husbands or sons.
highlights: Tax relief provided for NSmen and their wives and parents

sections.About this support:
- NSman Self Relief of $1,500 to $5,000 for eligible NSmen
- NSman Wife Relief of $750 for the wives of eligible NSmen
- NSman Parent Relief of $750 for each parent of the eligible NSman
sections.Who is this for?:
**NSman Self Relief:**

- Completed full-time National Service under the Enlistment Act or deemed to have completed such service by the proper authority
- Not a regular in the following organisations:
  - MINDEF
  - Singapore Police Force
  - Singapore Civil Defence Force
  - Central Narcotics Bureau
  - Singapore Prison Service
- Have not committed disciplinary or criminal offences in the preceding work year
- If you and your son are both NSmen, you will be eligible for either the NSman Self Relief or NSman Parent Relief, whichever is higher

**NSman Wife Relief:**

- You are a Singapore Citizen in the previous year
- Your husband is eligible for Nsman Self Relief
- Widows of deceased NSmen may also be eligible unless they have re-married

**NSman Parent Relief:**

- You are a Singapore Citizen in the previous year
- Your child is eligible for NSman Self Relief
- Your child was born to you and your spouse or ex-spouse / is your step-child / was legally adopted
- Parents of deceased NSmen are also eligible
- If you and your son are both NSmen, you will be eligible for either the NSman Self Relief or NSman Parent Relief, whichever is higher
- The relief amount per parent is capped at $750, regardless of how many children are NSmen
sections.How to apply?: No application is required. The relief will be automatically granted based on eligibility.

title: Family Service Centre (FSC)
description: FSCs provide support for vulnerable individuals and families with social and emotional issues, and work towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sections.About this support:
FSCs are community-based social services that provide support for vulnerable individuals and families with social and emotional issues. Social Work Practitioners at the FSCs provide case management support and also partner with other agencies to coordinate holistic support for clients to help them achieve stability, self-reliance, and social mobility.

FSC services include:

- Information and Referral: Providing information about social services, and linking individuals and families to appropriate social services and community resources based on the assessed needs
- Casework: Providing holistic case management and individual/family counselling
- Group Work: Bringing individuals and families with common needs together for purposeful group interactions to address their concerns and bring about positive change
- Community Work: Tapping on community resources to help individuals and families support and empower one another.
sections.Who is this for?:
FSCs are open to families and individuals:

- Regardless of age, race, language or religion;
- At different life stages (such as couples, families with young children, adolescents, or elderly members); and
- Of various family structures
sections.How to apply?:
Call, walk in or email the FSCs for help on family, socio-emotional, interpersonal or other social issues. 
To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, you can call ComCare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon contact with a FSC, a FSC worker will assess the needs of the individual/family and determine the type of support needed.
- If FSC services are required, the FSC will then work with the individual/family on their issues with the appropriate social work interventions.
- If the FSC’s services are not required and other supportive services by other partners can help to meet these needs, the FSC worker will refer the individual/family to appropriate social services or community resources.

title: Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR)
description: Provides tax relief for eligible working mothers, up to 25% of earned income per child. Encourages married women to stay in the workforce after having children, and rewards families with children who are Singapore Citizens.
highlights: Relief of up to 25% of working mother’s earned income per child or $12,000 per child
Receive cumulative tax relief for multiple children, up to 100% of your earnable income

sections.About this support:
- Up to 25% of the mother's earned income can be claimed as tax relief for each child
- Relief amount is cumulative for multiple children, capped at 100% of the mother's earned income
- Relief may be claimed alongside the Qualifying Child Relief (QCR) or Child Relief (Disability) on the same child
- The total relief cap is $50,000 per child for all 3 combined
sections.Who is this for?:
To be eligible for WMCR, you must fulfil all the following conditions in the previous year :

- You are a working mother who is married, divorced or widowed
- You have taxable earned income from employment, through pensions, trade or business, or via profession or vocation
- You have cared for a child who was a Singapore Citizen as at 31 December of the previous year and qualifies for QCR / Child Relief (Disability)
- You may read more on the [QCR and Child Relief (Disability) schemes and their criteria here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-child-relief-(disability)))
- You may still claim WMCR even for children who have passed away in the previous year
